articles.title: A step back: On Trump’s no-war, no-deal approach against Iran
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Trump must accept the realities of the war if he wants a deal

Before the November 3 midterm elections, U.S. President Donald Trump had repeatedly threatened to “destroy” Iran unless it entered into a deal with the U.S. to end the war. Since the elections, in which Mr. Trump’s Republican Party suffered a massive defeat , the U.S. President appears to have toned down his rhetoric. Last week, he said he had decided against escalating the military conflict with Iran following requests from America’s Gulf allies. But the U.S. would maintain the naval blockade of the Islamic Republic. Mr. Trump also pulled Vice President J.D. Vance off negotiations with Iran, as the Qatar-mediated talks made no real progress. Iran wants the U.S. to lift the blockade, unfreeze its frozen assets, issue sanctions relief and pull back from the Persian Gulf for direct negotiations on the nuclear programme to restart. The U.S., which calls Iran’s demands “outrageous”, has now adopted a no-war, no-deal approach , hoping that the economic blockade would force Tehran to offer concessions in the near future. Mr. Trump’s retreat from the threats reflects the realities on the ground. Before the U.S. and Israel launched this war by assassinating Iran’s Supreme Leader on February 28, Tehran was ready to make concessions. The U.S. and Israel carried out heavy bombing for 40 days but achieved none of their declared objectives. There is no guarantee that another round of strikes would force Iran to change its position. And the war, as the midterm results show, remains very unpopular in America.

Mr. Trump has only himself, and Benjamin Netanyahu, to blame for the predicament he is in. He is the one who sabotaged a functioning Obama-era nuclear deal in 2018 that had denied Iran a path towards the nuclear bomb. Mr. Trump joined Israel’s unprovoked war on Iran in June 2025 and declared that he had “obliterated” Iran’s nuclear programme. And the same Mr. Trump started the current war, just eight months later, over the same nuclear programme. The Iranian state has survived, though Iranians are facing enormous economic woes. Tehran shut the Strait of Hormuz, pumping up global energy prices. Iran’s counterattacks have either destroyed or damaged America’s bases in the Persian Gulf. High oil prices and inflation turned the American electorate against the Republican party, while in Israel, Mr. Netanyahu, despite war rhetoric and racist attacks on the country’s Arab minorities, lost the governing majority. The setbacks are there for anyone to see. Yet, Mr. Trump does not seem to have grasped the seriousness of the situation. His no-war, no-deal approach r isks a resumption of hostilities as Iran has pledged to break the siege. The U.S. has few clear military options unless it is prepared to launch a ground invasion, which would be disastrous. A more rational way forward is to end the war through diplomacy. But for that, Mr. Trump must first accept the strategic reality that he has lost the war.

articles.title: Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Congress should scale down its ambition while seeking an alliance with the SP

As Uttar Pradesh heads to the polls in early 2027, a familiar seat-sharing tussle has emerged within the Opposition. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress share an understanding forged during the Lok Sabha elections that earned them a good share of the State’s seats, but the Congress is now reportedly seeking 181 seats , nearly 45% of the 403 Assembly constituencies. It is the latest instance of the dilemma facing the Congress as it seeks revival in States where it has become a marginal force: how to strike a favourable bargain with stronger partners without weakening the coalition against the Bharatiya Janata Party. With discontent rising against the BJP, which still occupies a hegemonic position in the party system , the Opposition feels a wind behind its sails, and its major parties agree that the only way to take on the BJP is a formidable coalition with a compelling, unified message. But the Congress’s attempt to rebuild itself in the Hindi heartland and in States where it once held sway has strained that unity. In Bihar, the Mahagathbandhan failed to reap the benefits of anti-incumbency against the Janata Dal (United)-BJP alliance, partly because it could not tap the full support of the social forces behind the Rashtriya Janata Dal and the Congress, and partly because the Congress took too long to settle seat-sharing for the campaigns to gel. In Tamil Nadu, the Congress held out for more seats from the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam and delayed the alliance, while infighting produced a lacklustre campaign that left it with the lowest vote share, in the seats it contested, among the alliance partners.

Uttar Pradesh need not go the same way. The demand for 181 seats is overly ambitious for a party that managed a mere 2.33% of the votes in the 399 seats it contested in 2022, when the SP won 111 of the 347 seats it contested with a 32% vote share. The Congress has a point that the variables have changed since. In 2024, the SP and the Congress together won 43 of U.P.‘s 80 Lok Sabha seats with a 43.2% vote share, just short of the BJP-led alliance’s 43.7%. The Congress won only six of the 17 seats it contested, but its vote share in those six, 44.2%, was marginally ahead of the SP’s 43.4%. The party could also argue that its national campaigns on youth concerns and the state of India’s electoral democracy give it the heft to seek more. But its lack of an efficient State-wide organisation suggests that 181 is too high. The SP remains the strongest Opposition party , having assiduously built a new social coalition of backward classes, Dalits and minorities to take on the majoritarian BJP through local mobilisations. The 2024 arrangement, in which the Congress contested a fifth of the seats, is a more reasonable guide. A well-targeted 100 or so seats would make for a more coherent campaign and a better showing alongside the SP.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 17 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Plea in SC says ghost Form 7s haunt Mustafabad constituency during Delhi SIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The petition said persons declared dead were alive, while persons said to have shifted were found at home. Thirty-seven applications examined by the authorities were found to be false or fabricated.

Congress leader Ali Mehdi approached the Supreme Court on Monday alleging that Assembly Constituency-69 (AC-69) of Mustafabad is seeing a “substantial” amount of ghost Form 7s seeking deletion of voters in the ongoing Delhi SIR, and a crisis of electoral integrity is brewing.

The writ petition filed through advocate Shariq Ahmed, and highlighting multiple reports by The Hindu, said voters whose names feature for deletion on the grounds of death, absence and permanent shifting were found to be very much alive, present and staying put at their recorded addresses on the electoral roll.

The persons in whose names Form 7s have been filed for deletion of these voters deny having filed or signed on the applications. The petition alleged that ghost Form 7s seemed to have been filed by phantom objectors in the Mustafabad constituency.

“The integrity of an electoral roll is compromised not only when an ineligible name remains upon it. It is equally compromised when an eligible elector is removed from it on a fact which never existed or upon an objection which the supposed objector never made. The present record discloses the latter danger in its stark form,” the writ petition said.
It said persons declared dead were alive, while persons said to have shifted were found at home. Thirty-seven applications examined by the authorities were found to be false or fabricated.
“The existence of a genuine objector and the existence of a genuine ground for deletion — In Mustafabad, both are under serious doubt at the same time,” Mr. Ahmed submitted.

Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 requires the Electoral Registration Officer to be satisfied, after proper verification of the facts, before an entry can be corrected or deleted.

Rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection to the proposed inclusion of a name or an application for deletion to be made in Form 7 and to be preferred by a person whose own name is included in the electoral roll.
Form 7 requires identification of the applicant, identification of the elector objected to, the particular ground for deletion and a declaration as to the truth of the particulars stated.
The guidelines accompanying the form place the onus of substantiating the ground upon the applicant.

“There must be an identifiable person who has actually invoked the statutory process and there must be a factual ground capable of sustaining the deletion sought. If either fails, the foundation of the objection fails,” the petition said.

The petition drew attention to an investigation by The Hindu which reported that 28 electors against whom deletion applications had been submitted were physically traced to the addresses at which they were enrolled.

articles.title: 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit to kick off on November 17
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning

Karnataka is set to host the 29th edition of its flagship annual technology exposition, the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning.

Addressing a media conference on the eve of the summit, Minister for Home, IT & BT, and e-Governance Priyank Kharge said that the conference would feature over 120 knowledge sessions across 16 thematic tracks, including IT & DeepTech, Frontier Tech, Electro-Semicon, Electric Mobility, Health & Biotech, Digital Infrastructure & Data Centres, Data & Cybersecurity, Assistive Tech, Focus GCC, Circular Economy, Orange Economy, Finverse, Skilling & Edutech, India–USA Tech Conclave, Global Collaborations, and India Innovates.

Highlighting the summit’s global trajectory, Mr. Kharge noted how the expo has expanded over the decades to draw international participation. “Bengaluru Tech Summit has evolved beyond an annual technology gathering into a platform where global conversations translate into partnerships, investments, and tangible opportunities,” the Minister said.
The State’s ambition was to make Bengaluru a gateway for the world to engage with India’s technology ecosystem, while taking Karnataka’s innovations and solutions to global markets, he added.

According to Mr. Kharge, the 2026 edition introduces several new initiatives, including the debut of the GCC India Leaders’ Dialogue on Wednesday and a new Workshops & Masterclass Series featuring 11 sessions by global firms such as Nvidia, Cloudflare, and eBay. The summit will also host three co-located international events: the maiden edition of Germany’s embedded world India, alongside France-origin sustainability and health forums ChangeNOW and One Sustainable Health.

A 50,000 sq. ft. AI & Robotics Pavilion co-curated by Bharat1.ai, showcasing indigenous humanoids, drones, and India’s first quadrupedal athletic showcase, would be a new feature. The summit will also mark the launch of AI Kavach, the country’s first AI cybersecurity lab for the BFSI (banking, financial services and insurance) sector developed with IIT Kanpur.

Backed by Karnataka’s Global Innovation Alliance, which has expanded from 10 countries in 2018 to over 40 nations, the event will have Sweden as its Country Partner, alongside delegations from over 65 countries. Over 1,000 startups from 100 Indian cities will participate, culminating on November 19 with the Future Makers Conclave to celebrate 10 years of Karnataka’s ELEVATE initiative and felicitate recent unicorns and IPO achievers.

articles.title: DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The criminal case has been registered against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore. On Monday (November 16, 2026), DVAC officials launched a search at seven places and seized receipt vouchers for book procurement and other documents. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers, was arrested

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a criminal case against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore, over allegations of large-scale irregularities in the procurement of books.

The case was registered after prima facie evidence pointing to forgery, criminal conspiracy, and corruption was established in a detailed inquiry conducted on a complaint filed by the Secretary, School Education Department, who sought a probe into the alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for public libraries.
Investigation revealed that the “coordination committee” had added titles not recommended by the “books recommendation committee”, which had proposed around 26,000 books for purchase.
These additions were not brought on record in the official note file, the First Information Report said.

It also revealed that books were allegedly written in fictitious names, with plagiarised content and violations of the Transparent Book Procurement Policy, 2024, which prescribed a systematic, transparent, and structured procedure for the purchase of books for public libraries.

Besides the officials, the agency booked R. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers (also known as Akal Vilakku Pathippagam), and Phoenix Publications, both based at Madipakkam, Chennai, and other unidentified persons.

The DVAC said in its FIR that the State government had sanctioned ₹50 crore for procuring books and e-books for Periyar Arivulagam. The procurement was also intended to cover Kamarajar Arivulagam, Tiruchi; Bharathidasan Arivulagam, Salem; Anjalai Ammal Arivulagam, Cuddalore; Quaid-e-Millath Arivulagam, Tirunelveli; and libraries in six newly formed districts.

The agency said Mohan was the proprietor of both publishing firms that had operated from the same address and were associated with Sigma Prints and Sigma Publishing Services. He had given a list of 2,339 titles in the name of Akal Vizhakku Publishers and 99 titles in the name of Phoenix Publications. Purchase orders for 1,857 books were issued to the two publishers on February 13 and 14, 2026. After the books were received and verified, the list submitted by Akal Vizhakku Publishers was forwarded for processing payment for 1,779 books.

Investigators said Mohan had “created the books under fictitious author names, using information taken from websites and online applications, including ChatGPT. The contents were found to be vague, irrelevant and misleading, and of substandard language with no educational or informational value for a public library”.

The inquiry exposed instances of factually wrong information and plagiarism. One book described Naladiyar as a poet and philosopher, while another said the author of Madurai Kanchi was a king. The book titled Tourism: Principles, Practices and Philosophies, attributed to Emily Lawson, contained material copied from other books.

“The State government paid from public funds to the two publications for books which were written under false author names, in some cases copied from other works, and not fit for a public library,” the DVAC said.

The inquiry revealed that the procurement of books from Akal Vilakku Pathipagam and Phoenix Publications was done not only for Periyar Arivulagam but also for other public libraries at a cost of ₹1.74 crore. The investigation would be extended to unearth whether other publishers supplied similar books to the public libraries.

articles.title: Delhi car blast: SC allows transfer of cases to capital for joint trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed a plea by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for transfer of two criminal cases linked to the November 2025 car explosion near the Red Fort Metro station from Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana to a special court in the national capital.
A Bench headed by Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra also directed that three FIRs registered in the matter across Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana be clubbed together for a joint trial in Delhi.
A powerful explosion ripped through a slow-moving car at a traffic signal near the Red Fort Metro station on November 10, 2025, killing 12 people and injuring several others.

The apex court pointed to the overlapping of accused persons, witnesses and evidence, making separate trials in different States unfeasible. The court also took into consideration the security of the trial, with several accused persons still absconding.

All three cases were intricately connected and formed part of one overarching conspiracy, requiring a joint trial in one place.
Following the blast, several arrests were made, including that of four doctors. The alleged car bomber, Umar Nabi, was reported to be a doctor himself.

articles.title: Charge sheet against six in conspiracy to raise funds for TRF: police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mukhtar Ahmad Baba, a TRF-linked terrorist operating from Pakistan, used hawala and other covert channels to send funds into J&K, CIK stated

Counter Intelligence Kashmir (CIK), a special cell of the J&K Police, filed a charge sheet on Monday (November 16, 2026) against six people accused of a “conspiracy to raise and route funds to a banned outfit, The Resistance Front (TRF)” .
A CIK spokesman said the charge sheet was filed before the court of the Special Judge Designated Under NIA Act (TADA/POTA), Srinagar.

“Mukhtar Ahmad Baba, a TRF-linked terrorist operating from Pakistan, used hawala and other covert channels to send funds into J&K. Three Srinagar residents — Erfan Gul, Shazia Nazir, and Riyaz Ahmad Gojri — travelled to Saudi Arabia ostensibly for Umrah (pilgrimage). There they met Baba’s associates and received TRF funds to distribute among terrorists, separatists, and over-ground workers,” the CIK said.
The CIK claimed that digital devices containing key evidence were seized during searches. It said Gul, Nazir, and Gojri have been charged under BNS Sections 61(2), and 152, and UAPA Section 13.

The agency added that three other accused — Mohammad Iqbal Naima (based in Dubai), Shamima Shawl (London), and Mukhtar Ahmad Baba (Pakistan) — who are absconding, were charged under BNS Sections 61(2), and 152, alongside Sections 13, 38, 39 and 40 of the UAPA.

articles.title: J&K Finance Assistants exam: 14 held as cheating module busted in Jammu; mobiles, wireless sets seized, say police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly intended to facilitate the transmission of answers to candidates inside the examination halls, were found and seized by police

A cheating module, planning to employ unfair means by using mobile and wireless devices during the J&K Service Selection Board examination for the posts of Finance Assistants, was busted in Jammu, the J&K Police said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

“The police received information through live sources about people intending to indulge in unfair activity. Different teams were formed and the suspects were followed. These people reached different centres as our teams tracked them. Around the start of the examination, or even before it, the four modules were identified,” said Joginder Singh, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Jammu, during a press conference.

The examination for the posts was held on Sunday (November 15, 2026) in J&K. Mr. Singh said wireless sets and mobile phones were recovered from their possession. “The beneficiaries were identified. The police waited for the examination to end. Later, the beneficiaries were arrested as well. Electronic gadgets from them,” said Mr. Singh.
Mr. Singh said 14 persons were arrested, eight wireless sets and about 22 phones seized in the case. Five four-wheelers were also seized, officials said.
According to the police, the gang was working in two teams, one functioning inside the examination hall and the other from the outside.
“The question paper, or some questions, was conveyed to the outside team. The team outside would find its answer and communicate it back,” said the police officer.
Officials said three First Information Reports were registered in the case and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) has been constituted to probe it.
“Investigation into the complete modus operandi and use of gadgets is still going on,” said Mr. Singh.

Nearly 1.62 lakh aspirants had appeared for around 600 posts across J&K in the examination. “I keep thinking about the parents who borrowed money for these forms and the child who studied for months for a single chance. The question every candidate is asking is simple. Did any device reach inside a hall, and if it did, how?” said Opposition Peoples Democratic Party legislator Muntazir Mehdi.
He urged the JKSSB and the J&K Police “to come out with a clear statement and not a vague press note”.

“If anyone from inside the system is involved, they should be named and punished. Our youth have already lost too much faith in recruitment exams. This one has to be clean, and it has to be seen as clean,” said Mr. Mehdi.

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.
Similarly, the crude petroleum and natural gas segment saw inflation climb to 70.8% in October 2026 from 57.3% in September. This was compared to a 7.2% contraction in prices in October of last year.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

articles.title: Equity vs bonds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Concentrated bets in equity market could generate high returns if your bet turns right; On the other hand, diversification pays off for bond investments

Diversification may have its virtues but so does concentrated investments. Sector funds are examples of concentrated bets. In this article, we draw a distinction between concentrated bets in the equity and the bond markets and show why the former is meaningful and the latter, somewhat risky.

In theory, equity has unlimited upside potential. That means stock prices can rise to any level. In the real world, stock prices have high, not unlimited, upside potential given our finite investment horizon. Yet, concentrated bets can be meaningful. If you expect the banking sector to do well in the coming year, buying units of a banking sector ETF or a sector fund could be optimal. But the downside can be high if your bet turns wrong.
Macroeconomic & Financial Update: Equity vs bonds. This development reflects key trends in India's fiscal roadmap, monetary policy transmission, and financial sector resilience.

RBI & Fiscal Dynamics: In the context of inflation targeting by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), credit growth, capital expenditure (Capex), and external balance of payments remain vital indicators for economic stability.

articles.title: Need a quick loan? Beware of digital lending traps

fullParagraphs: From hidden charges and misuse of personal data to coercive recovery tactics, digital borrowing demands more than a cursory glance as borrowers need to know what the loan really costs

articles.title: Mahanagar Gas hikes CNG prices in Mumbai by ₹1.5/kg, sixth hike since May
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14
Amid rising costs of input gas, Mahanagar Gas Ltd (MGL) increased prices of compressed natural gas (CNG) at their retail outlets ₹1.5 per kg.
Effective November 15, CNG in Mumbai would be priced at ₹91.5 per kg in Mumbai.
Cumulatively prices of the vehicular gas have increased ₹9.5 per kg across six tranches since May 14.
Moreover, the latest is the second hike in the ongoing month.

The uncertainty in West Asia and the loss of supplies from Qatar, which is the world’s largest LNG producer and among the most reliable suppliers, have obligated purchasers to further alternate scouting of the natural gas and increasingly buy at spot.

In a statement, MGL said, “The ongoing Middle East crisis, coupled with reduced domestic gas allocation and increased dependence on higher-cost imported RLNG linked to international benchmarks, has significantly increased MGL’s gas procurement costs, particularly for the CNG segment, driven by strong demand and a higher share of imported gas in its input mix.”
Previously, privately-owned Adani Total Gas too have also hiked CNG prices at their outlets cumulatively by ₹6.75 per kg across two tranches since October 23.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Trump says ‘would not mind’ Huang being reinstated at Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Trump said Jensen Huang ‘learned a big lesson’ and he ‘would certainly not mind’ if he was reinstated, while adding that there’s a ‘big group of people that would like him to return’

Jensen Huang is reportedly trying to make a comeback as CEO of Nvidia as a campaign to reinstate him picked up steam Monday, with support from tech industry leaders as well as many of the chipmaker's employees.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who has been close with Mr. Huang, also suggested he could return to Nvidia. Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang “learned a big lesson” and he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.
There’s a “big group of people that would like him to return,” Mr. Trump added.
SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, CEO of video game maker Epic Games, were among thousands of people who signed an online petition calling for Huang to return to the company.

Mr. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.

Mr. Huang is plotting a comeback, the Financial Times reported over the weekend, citing multiple anonymous sources. The newspaper said he has been discussing the possibility with confidants, as his allies assembled a “war room” of Silicon Valley allies to lobby for his return.

The “Stand with Jensen” petition was set up Friday (November 13) and soon gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other supporters. It calls on the board to bring back Mr. Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or there's “compelling evidence” that his departure is in the company's best interests.

“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the petition's organizers said in an open letter. “We do not have access to the Board's private deliberations. We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.”
The identities of the signatories could not be independently verified, and the website said that their “affiliations are self-reported and not verified.”
Some people posted on their personal accounts that they supported the effort.
“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too,” Mr. Musk posted on X, while Mr. Sweeney wrote, “Save Jensen!”
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the petition.

Mr. Huang is plotting a comeback, the Financial Times reported over the weekend, citing multiple anonymous sources. The newspaper said he has been discussing the possibility with confidants, as his allies assembled a “war room” of Silicon Valley allies to lobby for his return.

The “Stand with Jensen” petition was set up Friday (November 13) and soon gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other supporters. It calls on the board to bring back Mr. Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or there's “compelling evidence” that his departure is in the company's best interests.

“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the petition's organizers said in an open letter. “We do not have access to the Board's private deliberations. We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.”

The identities of the signatories could not be independently verified, and the website said that their “affiliations are self-reported and not verified.”

Some people posted on their personal accounts that they supported the effort.

“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too,” Mr. Musk posted on X, while Mr. Sweeney wrote, “Save Jensen!”

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the petition.

fullParagraphs: India and Egypt have agreed to establish a joint working group to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement between the two countries, the government announced on Monday (November 16, 2026).

During his ongoing visit to Egypt, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal co-chaired, along with Egypt’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, the 7th session of the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.
This was the first time this JTC has been convened at the ministerial level.

“As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries,” the government said in a release.

“Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains,” the release said.
“India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships,” it added.

The committee also reviewed the growth in India-Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to $6.5 billion in 2025-26. Trade during the first half of the current financial year (April-September 2026) also stood at a little more than $5 billion, up 65% over its level in the same period of 2025.

articles.title: Divergent positions mark draft text of COP31 under way in Turkiye
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye.

Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively.

The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement.

The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change.

Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways.

Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions.

Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency.

COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

In his first statement at the conference, Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said the global just transition agenda — which involves moving workers from fossil-fuel-based industries towards renewable energy sectors — needed to move beyond dialogue and exchanges of experience towards practical, country-driven implementation. He reiterated India’s commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.

articles.title: Third American aircraft carrier arrives in West Asia as Trump keeps options open in Iran war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three, an unusually high number
The U SS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the West Asia, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three — an unusually high number.
A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations, on Monday (November 16, 2026) confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region.
It brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump has kept his options open during the more than 8-month-old Iran war.
The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September.

The Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as scores of smaller navy ships, that are in the region maintaining a blockade of Iranian shipping. The H.W. Bush arrived in the region in April while the George Washington arrived in August.
According to the Navy, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers as well as 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship.

articles.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group.

The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast.

People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area.
A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition.

The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported.
Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance.
The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.
Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.
Residents of Aden said government security forces had set up more checkpoints and were carrying ⁠out identity checks in the city, the government’s seat of power since the Houthis took Sanaa in 2014.

“Food supplies are available, and so is fuel. However, people are worried about the retreat of government forces and the ‌possibility of fighting drawing closer to Aden,” government employee Amin Mahmoud told Reuters by phone from the city.

articles.title: Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".

"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.
"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.

Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.

Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.

The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.

Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.

Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".

"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.

Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.

"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.

"Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now," he added.

articles.title: AIIMS Delhi performs a life-changing spinal repair in utero, before the patient’s first breath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: This is India’s first open foetal repair for myelomeningocele, a defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine; over 30 clinicians and nurses involved in multidisciplinary procedure

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi has performed India’s first open foetal repair of a lumbosacral myelomeningocele — the most severe form of spina bifida — at 25 weeks’ gestation.

“The six-hour operation repaired the cerebrospinal-fluid-leaking lumbosacral defect in utero. It followed more than five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, detailed foetal imaging, non-directive counselling, anaesthetic preparation, and operative simulation,’’ AIIMS said in a statement.
A myelomeningocele is an open neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine.

The patient was first screened and counselled by K. Aparna Sharma from the Maternal–Fetal Medicine team. The multidisciplinary procedure was performed using high-end microscopy and continuous high-end ultrasonography assistance at the Neurosciences Centre. The procedure was provided free of cost to the family under the Union government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK).

Deepak Gupta, who led the neurosurgical component, said that the intervention was done after rigorous selection. “Prenatal repair seeks to limit ongoing injury to exposed neural tissue, reduce the subsequent need for cerebrospinal-fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, and improve selected neurological outcomes. It is not a cure, and long-term multidisciplinary care remains essential,” he said.

More than 30 clinicians and nurses from the Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Maternal–Fetal Medicine, Neurosurgery, Obstetrics and Neuroanaesthesia, Plastic Surgery, Radiodiagnosis, Neonatology, and Nursing teams of the Neurosciences Centre and Obstetrics–Gynaecology services participated in the procedure.

Professor Aparna Sharma added that this foetal intervention was well-reasoned and a planned decision aimed to optimise the outcomes of both the baby and the mother. The safety of both mother and foetus was ensured through detailed counselling, high-quality anaesthesia, and coordinated surveillance before and after surgery.

“International trial evidence supports prenatal repair in carefully selected foetuses with open myelomeningocele. The procedure nevertheless carries important maternal and foetal risks, including prematurity and uterine-scar complications, and must be performed only in specialised centres,’’ she said.

The team emphasised that foetal surgery is a treatment for selected pregnancies, not a substitute for prevention. Neural-tube closure occurs by approximately 28 days after conception, often before pregnancy is recognised. Pre-conception folic-acid counselling, evidence-based food fortification with folates, and robust national surveillance remain essential to reducing India’s burden of neural tube defects.

“The mother and foetus will continue to receive close multidisciplinary surveillance through pregnancy, delivery, and the newborn period,’’ the AIIMS statement said, adding that a child with spina bifida may begin life with paralysis, hydrocephalus, and lifelong challenges.

Traditionally, neurosurgeons have done this operation after the child is born. But by then, some of the neurological damage may already have occurred. For some children with spina bifida, the opportunity to protect the spinal cord now begins before birth.

articles.title: Matrescence: when motherhood needs mental health support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: At least one in five women will experience mental health problems during pregnancy until till the first year after childbirth. This cannot be ignored any longer: we need better, more comprehensive policies and programmes to support mothers during this vulnerable period

Monica was not prepared for a caesarean section. She had done everything right and had been assured of a vaginal delivery. Then two weeks before the expected date of delivery, she had to be rushed to the emergency for a caesarean. Monica felt that she had completely lost control of the situation. She found herself alone in an intensive care ward away from her baby, who was in the neonatal ICU and described her birth experience as being extremely traumatic. She is now unable to bond with her baby and keeps questioning herself. Am I such a terrible mother? Will I be like this lifelong?

Priya became pregnant after multiple IVF procedures but did not disclose the pregnancy to anyone till the third trimester, as she didn’t want to jinx it. After a healthy baby girl was born, Priya continued to be anxious and could not trust anyone else to take care of the baby. She would be hypervigilant, and even the smallest change in the infant’s spit-up or breathing would make her panic.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Matrescence: when motherhood needs mental health support. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: 29-year-old regains limb movement after emergency stroke treatment at two govt. hospitals
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A 29-year-old woman from Manuguru, who was rushed to hospital after suddenly losing movement in her right arm and leg, regained significant mobility within hours after doctors at two government hospitals coordinated to administer emergency stroke treatment within the critical window.

Rajani’s ordeal began on an ordinary morning when she suddenly developed slurred speech and complete weakness on her right side. Recognising the signs of an acute stroke, doctors acted swiftly to prevent permanent brain damage.

She was first taken to Area Hospital, Manuguru, where Sai Kumar, a General Medicine specialist, identified the symptoms and arranged an urgent referral to Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, nearly 60 km away, for emergency treatment.

Recognising the narrow window for intervention, M. Ramakrishna, medical superintendent of Area Hospital, Manuguru, coordinated directly with Tejaswi Gadde, physician at Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, to facilitate her transfer.

At Bhadrachalam, doctors immediately conducted a CT scan to rule out bleeding in the brain before administering clot-dissolving medication. With Rajani still within the recommended 4.5-hour treatment window, doctors administered intravenous Tenecteplase at 2 p.m., around 3.5 hours after the symptoms began, said G. Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS), Bhadradri Kothagudem.

The response to treatment was encouraging. Before the intervention, Rajani had no detectable movement in her right arm or leg, with her muscle power recorded at 0/5. Following thrombolysis, her muscle strength improved, and she regained the ability to move the affected limbs against resistance, though full strength is yet to return.

She remains under close neurological observation. The case also highlights the availability of advanced emergency treatment in government hospitals serving remote and tribal areas. The thrombolytic medication, which costs around ₹45,000 in the market, was administered to Rajani free of cost.

Dr. Ravi Babu appreciated the doctors, nurses and supporting staff at both hospitals for their prompt decisions and coordination. “Such interventions demonstrate how teamwork between government healthcare institutions can help deliver advanced, life-saving treatment even in geographically remote areas,” he said.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).
