articles.title: Pollution in Yamuna increased despite huge expenditure on cleaning: Supreme Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: “This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna,” said SC

Pollution in Yamuna has only increased despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, the Supreme Court has said, directing the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) to monitor water quality at the points where the Yamuna and its major drains enter and exit states, Union territories and districts.

In an order dated November 4, a Bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Manmohan observed that industrial pollutants and untreated sewage must be stopped at the source, and merely constructing more sewage treatment plants is not sufficient to clean the river.

"This court is of the opinion that everything that is wrong with the civic administration in towns, cities and villages situated along the banks of the river is reflected in the poor health of the river and in the 520 drains that discharge wastewater into the Yamuna. This is why, despite huge sums being spent on cleaning the river, pollution in the Yamuna has only increased," the Bench said while hearing a plea related to cleaning of the river.
The top court said industrial pollution and untreated sewage must be curtailed, if not stopped altogether, at the source.

"Where that is not possible, the sewage must first be tapped and then treated. However, tapping will remain a challenge in absence of a robust sewage system and due to joining of stormwater and sewage drains.

"This court is further of the opinion that it would be difficult, if not impossible, for civic authorities to tap sewage in most illegal and unauthorised colonies built on encroached land, since they have not been built on a grid layout and have hardly any space for laying a sewage system," it said.

The apex court said unless illegal and unauthorised colonies and 'jhuggi-jhopdi' (slum) clusters on the drains as well as on the river bed are removed, with rehabilitation of their occupants, their sewage will continue to pollute the river.
The court directed that if water quality deteriorates while passing through a particular state, Union territory or district, the concerned authorities would be held accountable and penalised.
ALSO WATCH Every Chhath, the same question returns: Why is the Yamuna still polluted?

"If the water quality deteriorates on any parameter while flowing through, or exiting a state/Union territory or a district therein, that state/Union territory or district... shall be held accountable and penalised. The said compensation/ fine shall be deposited with the registry of this court," the Bench said, directing CPCB to suggest a formula for calculating the said compensation.

The top court also directed the CPCB to investigate and submit a detailed report with respect to any incident of pollution in the Yamuna, such as fish deaths, floating of white foam on the surface, eutrophication or algal bloom, or increase in Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD), Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD), or Total Suspended Solids (TSS) levels.
"The report should specifically mention the cause of such an incident or spike in pollution levels as well as remedial measures to be undertaken," it said.

articles.title: India scrutinises Red Bull’s sugar levels as ‘energy drink’ dispute escalates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation, the FSSAI said in the document

India is scrutinising the composition of Red Bull, the drink made by the eponymous Austrian company, warning the product’s “energy drink” label could encourage people to consume too much added sugar, an official notice showed, opening a new front in the regulator’s fight over food safety standards.

It is the first time India has raised health concerns and questioned companies on the ingredients of their energy drinks in a dispute that began in June and has triggered legal challenges in the Delhi High Court.

In a confidential notice to Red Bull on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) targeted the drink’s “nutritional composition”, saying it derived a significant proportion of its declared energy from the “substantial” amount of added sugar.
“The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation,” the FSSAI said in the document, which was reviewed by Reuters.

The notice gives Red Bull seven days to explain why India should not prohibit its use of the “energy drink” label given it had the “potential to mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption of added sugar.”
Red Bull and the FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

India’s energy drinks market is set to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, with sales growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, according to Euromonitor. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago.

Health experts are concerned energy drinks contain high levels of sugar, caffeine and taurine, an amino acid that research suggests can contribute to health problems. The drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

In court in recent weeks, Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the June order banning the label “energy drinks”, saying they were not given any advance notice of the strict action.

However, while Red Bull managed to secure a temporary court injunction to enable it to continue using the “energy drink” label, its competitors were told that once they sold their existing stock they had to stop using the label.

The regulator has asked the Delhi judge to review the Red Bull decision because it says it gives the company “an undue commercial advantage” against its rivals, according to its October court filing reviewed by Reuters. That challenge will be heard in January.

In its latest notice, the FSSAI said Red Bull’s beverage carried a consumption advisory indicating the product should not be consumed in quantities exceeding 500 millilitres a day, which it said could confuse consumers into believing it was fine to consume that quantity.

articles.title: Brace for impact: On rising inflation and external factors
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: High inflation due to external factors could soon exacerbate economic pain

India’s much-hyped domestic economic resilience is set to be tested over the next few months as external factors start to impose inescapable pressures. A case in point is inflation. The latest data on retail inflation show that it crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s 6% upper comfort limit in October 2026. According to economists, this is likely to continue through the third quarter of this financial year, which means at least two more months of high inflation. Agricultural shortfalls brought on by a patchy and deficient monsoon have meant that food inflation rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026. Elevated fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose sharply. What is worse is that high inflation is spreading to almost every aspect of a household’s day-to-day needs. In fact, the latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) data show that 10 of the 12 major categories saw inflation in October, hitting their highest levels recorded in the new series of the index. So, things such as clothing, footwear, housing, furnishings, and services such as healthcare, education, communication, recreation, and restaurant and hospitality are not only getting more expensive, but they are doing so at an accelerating rate. This would have been bad enough had wages been increasing in real terms. Yet, the latest research by Data for India on the country’s official wage statistics shows that, while nominal wages doubled from 2012 to 2024, they actually fell 4% over the same period after adjusting for inflation. And this is sharper for high-skilled and high-earning workers. Lower wage earners saw marginal increases over this period. While this is of some comfort, it is the higher wage earners that drive consumption in an economy. Real wage contraction for them, which is likely to have worsened in 2026, will hit consumption levels and private investment.

Further, there is strong evidence to suggest that the official inflation metrics are not capturing the full extent of rising prices. Data on cash with the public and UPI transactions show the value of both has been growing in double digits over the last year and more, significantly outpacing nominal GDP growth. This either suggests that the informal economy is far larger than earlier thought or, more likely, that inflation is well above what the official figures are being able to capture. Unfortunately, there are no real magic-wand fixes to this situation. Inflation is largely beyond the government’s control, and wage growth cannot happen overnight. The only way forward is to continue trying to spur sector-specific growth and warn people of the impending storm.

articles.title: Critical ban: On recycling of lithium-ion batteries

fullParagraphs: India needs to create an entire ecosystem for recycling of lithium-ion batteries

On November 10, the Directorate General of Foreign Trade banned the export of lithium-ion battery black mass by moving it from the “free” to the “prohibited” list of exports. Black mass is an intermediate product when spent batteries and factory scrap are shredded. It contains valuable lithium, nickel, cobalt, manganese and graphite. The Commerce Ministry says the ban will ensure feedstock for domestic refiners, lift their capacity utilisation and draw investment. While the recycling of lead-acid batteries end-to-end is an established ecosystem and formalised, too, lithium-ion battery recycling is an emerging segment with only a few dozen licensed operators but has much potential given the scale of use of such batteries in EVs. While the ban will redirect supply, it will not automatically create a market and ecosystem. Just banning export without creating an entire ecosystem will only lead to dumping of lithium-ion batteries into landfills if the blackmass has no market. Blackmass production is a largely mechanical process but further downstream processing is more specialised chemical processing requiring larger investment and further policy support. If downstream units are online, their output can directly feed into indigenous lithium-ion battery manufacture.

India depends heavily on imports for critical minerals such as those used in battery inputs. Beyond working on supply aspects, the government must address the price gap to create a robust recycling market. Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022, producers buy extended producer responsibility (EPR) certificates from recyclers but these are undervalued. Cheap certificates reward recycling on paper over investment in high-yield plants. A floor price that covers the full cost of recovery, with digital tracking, would fix that. Rare earths show how recycling remains a missed opportunity for India because of policy gaps. A smartphone can be up to 1% neodymium-iron-boron magnet by weight. That puts its rare earth content at about 3,000 parts per million, comparable to India’s monazite beach sands. Extracting it takes less energy than mining. A magnet separated from the phone is about 30% rare earth. Magnets make up as much as 3% of a hard drive, but are usable only if they are removed before the drive is shredded for data destruction. Yet the e-waste rules do not require rare earth separation. Rare earths need a separate EPR category, too. Payment by weight cannot be applied for rare earth minerals.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Plea in SC says ghost Form 7s haunt Mustafabad constituency during Delhi SIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The petition said persons declared dead were alive, while persons said to have shifted were found at home. Thirty-seven applications examined by the authorities were found to be false or fabricated.

Congress leader Ali Mehdi approached the Supreme Court on Monday alleging that Assembly Constituency-69 (AC-69) of Mustafabad is seeing a “substantial” amount of ghost Form 7s seeking deletion of voters in the ongoing Delhi SIR, and a crisis of electoral integrity is brewing.

The writ petition filed through advocate Shariq Ahmed, and highlighting multiple reports by The Hindu, said voters whose names feature for deletion on the grounds of death, absence and permanent shifting were found to be very much alive, present and staying put at their recorded addresses on the electoral roll.

The persons in whose names Form 7s have been filed for deletion of these voters deny having filed or signed on the applications. The petition alleged that ghost Form 7s seemed to have been filed by phantom objectors in the Mustafabad constituency.

“The integrity of an electoral roll is compromised not only when an ineligible name remains upon it. It is equally compromised when an eligible elector is removed from it on a fact which never existed or upon an objection which the supposed objector never made. The present record discloses the latter danger in its stark form,” the writ petition said.
It said persons declared dead were alive, while persons said to have shifted were found at home. Thirty-seven applications examined by the authorities were found to be false or fabricated.
“The existence of a genuine objector and the existence of a genuine ground for deletion — In Mustafabad, both are under serious doubt at the same time,” Mr. Ahmed submitted.

Section 22 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 requires the Electoral Registration Officer to be satisfied, after proper verification of the facts, before an entry can be corrected or deleted.

Rule 13(2) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 requires an objection to the proposed inclusion of a name or an application for deletion to be made in Form 7 and to be preferred by a person whose own name is included in the electoral roll.
Form 7 requires identification of the applicant, identification of the elector objected to, the particular ground for deletion and a declaration as to the truth of the particulars stated.
The guidelines accompanying the form place the onus of substantiating the ground upon the applicant.

“There must be an identifiable person who has actually invoked the statutory process and there must be a factual ground capable of sustaining the deletion sought. If either fails, the foundation of the objection fails,” the petition said.

The petition drew attention to an investigation by The Hindu which reported that 28 electors against whom deletion applications had been submitted were physically traced to the addresses at which they were enrolled.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Nations must deliver on past promises before committing to lofty climate goals

The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 16 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Caste and class: On OBC reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: India's exports up 29.9% in October; trade deficit narrows to $20.09 billion
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The growth in India’s merchandise exports in October, the fastest in five years and faster than import growth, indicates that volumes of exports are growing along with prices
India’s merchandise exports rose to an all-time high of $49.5 billion in October 2026, bringing down the country’s overall trade deficit, official data released on Friday showed.
While a large part of this growth was due to petroleum products, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said diversification of exports to various locations helped improve the numbers.
India’s total exports, including goods and services, stood at $89.99 billion in October 2026, up nearly 30% from last October.
The overall trade deficit shrank from $25.1 billion last October to $20.1 billion year-on-year.

“In the month of October, the exports of merchandise exports have registered a new peak of $49.47 billion,” Mr. Agrawal said at a press briefing. “This is the highest-ever monthly merchandise export value, along with the highest monthly growth of 45.03% in the last five years.”
Merchandise imports rose to a record high of $89.35 billion in October 2026, up 16.5% YoY. Total imports stood at $110.1 billion, a 16.6% increase.

According to trade experts, goods exports growing faster than merchandise imports shows that while the rise in global prices contributed to the increase in the value of India’s exports, there was also an increase in the underlying export volumes.

“The particularly encouraging part of this growth is that this is not in any particular sector, this is not in any particular geography, it is broad-based across countries and regions,” Mr. Agrawal added. “43 of our 50 top export destinations posted positive growth in October 2026 as compared to 2025.”
The data show that India’s exports to 12 out of its top 20 export destinations grew by double digits or more.
Mr. Agrawal pointed out that India’s exports to its free trade agreement (FTA) partners had grown strongly.
One of the key areas of diversification has been the African continent, with exports to that region growing 44% in April-September 2026 to $31.4 billion.
Notably, India’s trade with West Asia is recovering as countries find alternate routes and ports other than those along the constrained Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The RBI has reportedly proposed a ₹50 lakh sub-limit within the $250,000 annual Liberalised Remittance Scheme cap to curb dollar outflows and protect the rupee

The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Rampur Bushahr’s Lavi Fair in Himachal Pradesh traces a Himalayan journey from wool and barter to women entrepreneurs and digital payments

What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house

Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

fullParagraphs: A local resident has filed the case claiming that the inhabitants of two hamlets were facing hardship because of restrictions imposed on using the private road which was their only access to the outside world

A resident of Kodanad in Kothagiri taluk of the Nilgiris district has filed a public interest litigation petition in the Madras High Court seeking a direction to the Collector to acquire certain lands from the management of Kodanad Estate, owned by former Chief Minister Jayalalithaa during her lifetime, for use as a public road to access two hamlets located behind the estate.

The plea has been listed for hearing before the first Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan on Monday (November 16, 2026). P. Ganesan, 61, a farmer from the hamlets named Anna Nagar and Kamaraj Nagar had filed the case urging the district administraton to acquire the lands required for converting the 2.5 km long private road into a public road.

The petitioner said the Kodanad Estate management had permitted the inhabitants of the two hamlets to pass through the estate for many years by imposing restrictions such as obtaining permission from the Estate manager and upon payment of a nominal fee towards toll charges. When the order was taken on appeal, the Supreme Court in 2011 directed the estate management to permit access to the road even during night hours and restrained the management from locking both ends of the road. Stating that the residents were still facing hardship, the petitioner now said that the issue could be resolved only if the State acquires the lands required for converting the private road into a public road.

articles.title: NCW calls for inquiry, seeks report from DGP over Kallakurichi issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Commission for Women (NCW) has written to the Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police seeking a fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations that “C. Arul Vignesh, MLA from Kallakurichi, Tamil Nadu, sent obscene WhatsApp messages to J.E. Padmaja, District Collector, Kallakurichi.”

The NCW in a social media post said its chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar has written to the DGP, Tamil Nadu, seeking a “fair and impartial enquiry into the allegations, including examination of the representations reportedly made by the District Collector to senior officials and the action taken thereon.”

The Commission, which took suo motu cognisance of a media report, has called for the preservation and examination of relevant digital evidence and emphasised that the matter must be investigated without any political or external influence, irrespective of the position held by the person concerned, according to its social media post.

“The Commission has sought a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within seven days. The dignity, safety and security of women public officials must be upheld without exception. No position or influence can place anyone above accountability for alleged harassment or misconduct,” it said.

articles.title: Anbumani seeks pay hike for guest lecturers from Sept. 1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss on Sunday demanded that the monthly hike of ₹5,000 announced by the State government for guest lecturers, which would increase their salary from ₹30,000 to ₹35,000, be provided from September 1 instead of November 1.

“Higher Education Minister Viswanathan assured [the Assembly] that the salary hike would be implemented retrospectively from September. It is unjustifiable that guest lecturers are being let down despite this assurance. At a time when guest lecturers are being paid very low salaries, delaying even this modest hike is an injustice to them,” he said.

He also urged the government to increase their salary to ₹50,000 next year, in keeping with the recommendations of the University Grants Commission. “The Tamil Nadu government must also promptly fulfil all their other demands, including PF benefits, medical insurance, maternity leave for women guest lecturers, and a gratuity of ₹25 lakh upon retirement,” he said.

articles.title: CIAL sets up facilitation centre for Sabarimala pilgrims
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan to inaugurate the facility on November 17

Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) has set up a dedicated pilgrim facilitation centre at the airport for Sabarimala pilgrims. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will inaugurate the centre on November 17.

Spread across 5,000 sq. ft., the centre is located near the police aid post, adjacent to the domestic arrival terminal and will remain open round the clock. KSRTC bus services are available to and from the airport from here, with a booking counter set up at the centre. Pilgrims can also book chartered bus services on demand. A dedicated counter for helicopter service bookings has also been arranged.

The other facilities at the centre include a Devaswom help desk, prasadam coupon counter, prepaid taxi booking facility, vegetarian food outlet, and a rest area. A flight information display system has also been installed to provide real-time flight updates. Its proximity to the domestic terminal makes the centre easily accessible to pilgrims, says an official release.
Around 11,000 pilgrims made use of the facilitation centre last year, including those from Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Malaysia, and Singapore, it says.

articles.title: About 70 km of GCC roads to be handed over to Highways
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Arcot Road, Usman Road and Nelson Manickam Road are some of the key roads being transferred. Most of them are bus route roads linked to highways located within the city limits, says a source

The Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) is handing over key roads in Chennai, including Arcot Road, Usman Road, Nelson Manickam Road, Tondiarpet High Road, New Avadi Road, and Madhavaram Milk Colony Road, the State Highways Department.
Around 70 km of roads and portions of roads are on the list prepared by the corporation.

“They are being transferred since most of them are major bus route roads, which are contiguous with or connected to highways located within the city limit. It is for better administrative efficiency and maintenance. We have sent the proposal to the State government,” an official source in the GCC said.
The civic body will not get any road in exchange, as it did the last time it handed over some road stretches to the Highways.

The roads that are to be taken over are quite long, including Dr. MGR Salai-Arcot Road (6.4 km), Konnur High Road that is 5.4 km, New Avadi Road (5.2 km), and Tondiarpet High Road (4.8 km). The longest is the 7.21-km Kodambakkam-Sriperumbudur Road (Arcot Road).
Official sources in the Highways said works such as profile corrections of roads, restoration of road surfaces, and construction of storm-water drains would be carried out.
“We plan to introduce five-year performance-based maintenance contracts (PBMC) for these roads. The maintenance will be done by the same contractor who does the profile correction,” a source said.
The PBMC, in its earlier avatar, was introduced ten years ago, and given to contractors other than those who laid the roads.

articles.title: Hyderabad hospital performs combined heart valve procedures in single sitting
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Doctors at Apollo Hospitals in Hyderabad performed Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) and Balloon Mitral Valvotomy (BMV) on an 83-year-old man in a single sitting on Saturday.

The procedure was performed by cardiologists P.C. Rath and Manoj Kumar Agarwala during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting. The patient, who had previously undergone coronary artery bypass surgery and pacemaker implantation, was admitted with severe aortic and mitral valve stenosis.

Doctors opted for a minimally invasive intervention involving the replacement of the aortic valve and balloon dilatation of the mitral valve. Both procedures were successfully performed through the femoral artery, accessed through the groin, under anaesthesia. The intervention was also demonstrated live during the Hyderabad Valve Meeting.

Hyderabad is hosting leading interventional cardiologists and structural heart specialists from all over the world for Hyderabad Valves 2026, the fourth edition of a biennial scientific meeting focused on modern, minimally invasive treatments for heart valve disease.
The meeting brought together Indian and international experts for live case demonstrations, specialist lectures and interactive discussions on complex valve and structural heart interventions.

The conference features 26 live transcatheter cases from centres in India and overseas. The programme includes 11 live-case transmissions from leading international centres, including four from the USA, and six each from Europe and Apollo Hospitals, Jubilee Hills. Each demonstration provides an opportunity for specialists to discuss clinical decisions, procedural techniques and patient safety.

articles.title: Boy electrocuted by snapped stay wire in Malappuram; Minister orders probe
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 13-year-old boy died of electrocution after coming into contact with a snapped stay wire attached to an electric pole in a paddy field in Malappuram on Sunday (November 15).
The deceased, identified as Junaid, son of Shihabudheen of Cherumukku in Tirurangadi, had gone to the field with friends to watch a tractor plough the land, the police said.

Residents said Junaid’s friends tried to rescue him, but the tractor driver stopped them from approaching the wire, saving them from a similar fate. They alleged that officials of the Keralam State Electricity Board (KSEB) took time to disconnect the power supply despite repeated calls for help.
The incident triggered protests by residents who accused KSEB officials of serious negligence.
Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an immediate inquiry into the incident and directed officials to ensure compensation for the bereaved family.

In a statement, Mr. Joseph said that he had directed the Deputy Chief Engineer of KSEB, Tirurangadi, to submit a factual report immediately. “Strict disciplinary action will be taken against those found responsible for any lapse,” he added.
The Minister said safety inspections would be intensified across the State to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.
Meanwhile, the KSEB, in a statement, apologised for the incident and said that an impartial and detailed inquiry into the circumstances leading to the accident would be conducted.
The KSEB urged consumers to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details through WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

articles.title: My entire life has been a struggle, says Bilkis Bano at GIO conference in Kochi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage.

“My entire life has been a struggle,” Bilkis Bano, the Gujarat riots survivor who has emerged as an icon of resilience with her prolonged legal battle for justice, said in Kochi on Sunday (November 15).
Ms. Bano made the compelling remark as she inaugurated the International Conference on Women organised by the State committee of the Girls Islamic Organisation (GIO) in the city.

“Everyone knows my life story, don’t they? There is no need to say anything more about it,” she said in a brief address. Ms. Bano was gang-raped and lost seven members of her family, including her three-year-old daughter, in the 2002 riots.
Thanking those who invited her, she said, “May we continue to live with such love and peace every day, staying together all our lives.”

Her husband, Patel Yakub Rasool, who attended the conference, recollected the long and arduous struggle for justice she had to wage. “The family had to relocate several times, and her rights were denied. They had to repeatedly bring instances of injustice to the attention of those in positions of power. What happened to Bilkis is now known to the entire world. May her struggle inspire every woman to find the strength to raise her voice for her rights,” he said.
The conference was presided over by GIO State president K. Shifana. Jamia Millia Islamia student leader Nousheen Farooq was the chief guest.

Saria Cheruvallil, Professor at Coventry University, UK; Dalia Saleh, researcher at the University of Cambridge; Reem Mahmoud Al Haddad, Palestinian writer and journalist; Jamaat-e-Islami national secretary A. Rahmathunnisa; and Jamaat-e-Islami Keralam ameer P. Mujeeb Rahman were among those who spoke at various sessions.

articles.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet Modi in New Delhi this week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The couple will arrive in Mumbai today for the annual Earthshot Prize; the visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry

The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Katherine (Kate), are due to arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening (November 17) at a ceremony in the city. The couple will stay in Mumbai for the duration of their visit, which ends on Wednesday night (November 18, 2026).

The visit will involve events focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly,​ Brian Lara and England captain ​Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by Prince William in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crores) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.
India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody ), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s (November 17, 2026) event .
When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest of 15,000 schools across 24 States.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and Princess Kate’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

articles.title: Guest teachers in Haryana hold mock Assembly, demand regularisation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Guest teachers in Haryana schools held a mock Assembly at the Mini Secretariat in Kurukshetra on Saturday, demanding regularisation under the three-year policy notified in 2014 in accordance with court orders.

Organised on the call of the Rajkiya Anubandhit Adhyapak Sangh, the symbolic Assembly passed a resolution seeking regularisation of guest teachers by an overwhelming majority. The resolution will be submitted to Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini at his camp office in Kurukshetra on November 29. The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President.

Teachers said guest teachers had been serving in government schools for the past 21 years and contributing to the State’s education system, but the government continued to keep them in temporary employment arrangements instead of regularising their services. Following the court orders, the Haryana School Education Department issued speaking orders denying regular status to the guest teachers.
They said the mock Assembly was organised to raise questions concerning the regularisation of guest teachers, judicial decisions and the government’s accountability on a public platform.

The event was attended by educationists, intellectuals, employee union leaders from various departments, School Management Committee representatives, the Samyukt Kisan Morcha, student and youth organisations, advocates’ unions, writers’ associations, university professors, the Jan Sangharsh Manch, Kurukshetra, and social activists.
These teachers, appointed between 2005 and 2008, are working as junior basic teachers, trained graduate teachers, and post graduate teachers.

The teachers will also hold a rally in Delhi on December 12 and submit the resolution to the President.

articles.title: Diljit says attempts made to stop his Indore concert, recites ‘kisi ke baap ka Hindostan thodi hai’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an aggressive tone, the Punjabi artist appeared to take a dig at the political opposition to his Aura India Tour 2026

Singer Diljit Dosanjh took the stage for his concert in Madhya Pradesh’s Indore on Sunday and recited the famous couplet of poet Rahat Indori, “Kisi ke baap ka Hindostan thodi hai (India does not belong to anyone’s father),” amid security concerns and objections around the event. Mr. Dosanjh also claimed that he had come to Indore despite “several attempts being made to stop” him from performing in the city.

In an aggressive tone, the Punjabi artist also appeared to take a dig at the political opposition to his Aura India Tour 2026, which was kicked off with the concert in Indore’s Delight Dastoor ground.
“ Ye nahi gana hai, vo nahi gana hai. Ye nahi kar sakte, vo nahi kar sakte (You can’t sing this, you can’t sing that. You can’t do this, you can’t do that,” he said.
Mr. Dosanjh then recited the lines by Rahat Indori, who hailed from the city.

“Humare munh se jo nikle wahi sadaqata hai, hamare munh mein tumhari zuban thodi hai. Agar khilaf hain hone do, oye jaan thodi hai. Yeh sab dhuan hai koi aasman thodi hai. Main jaanta hoon ki dushman bhi kam nahin, lekin hamari tarah hatheli pe jaan thodi hai (Whatever passes my lips is the truth; I do not carry your words in my mouth. If there are those who oppose me, let them—it is not a matter of life and death. All this is merely smoke, not the vast sky. I know my enemies are formidable, but they do not hold their lives in the palms of their hands as I do),” he said.

The singer ended the couplet in high energy, saying, “Sabhi ka khoon hai shamil yahan ki mitti men, kisi ke baap ka hindustan thodi hai! ( The blood of all has mingled with this soil; India is not the private property of anyone’s father!)”
Asking the crowd to chant ‘Jai Shri Mahakal’, Mr. Dosanjh said that he was not afraid and that nobody could stop him from coming here.

“People of Indore, this is the land of Mahakal, and nobody can stop us from coming here. We weren’t afraid earlier and aren’t afraid today. And where is the question of you being afraid? It is your strength that has brought us here today,” he said.
“Although many attempts were made to stop me from coming here, I still came. Once I tell someone that I will come, I never back out. Despite all the restrictions, I am standing here,” he asserted.

Mr. Dosanjh’s concerts in cities like Indore and Gujarat’s Ahmedabad have faced objections from child protection authorities over songs involving liquor consumption, with the Indore District Child Protection Officer prohibiting four such songs in a November 6 order. The final permissions for the concerts also arrived from the local police just hours before the show.
Meanwhile, emails threatening bomb blasts at his concert were also received by the Indore Mayor’s office and other institutions, which were declared a hoax by the police following a brief probe.
In recent years, Mr. Dosanjh and his concerts in India have also faced heat from various right-wing groups over his political views and allegations that his songs promote intoxication and violence.

articles.title: Kerala Police find similarities between Gurumurthy, Kochi synagogue arson cases; yet to find evidence of Lawrence Bishnoi links
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thrissur police are investigating case against Tamil Nadu native Gurumurthy who was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks, while NIA has taken over probe into arson case

The police in Keralam have found similarities between the case in which a Tamil Nadu native was arrested recently from Palakkad for alleged links with criminal networks and the arson attack allegedly targeting a synagogue in Ernakulam.

Initial investigations have revealed similarities in the modus operandi of 27-year-old Gurumurthy, who was arrested from Ottappalam, Palakkad, on November 12, and Ebin P. Paul, 32, who has been remanded in judicial custody since his arrest for allegedly setting fire to a plant nursery located in front of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Ernakulam on October 12, State Police Chief Ravada A. Chandrasekhar said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Though the accused in both cases were suspected to have links with the infamous Lawrence Bishnoi gang, the police said they were yet to find evidence of any direct connection between the accused and the group.
The Thrissur police are investigating the case against Gurumurthy, while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the probe into the arson case.

“Initial investigation revealed that Gurumurthy was taking assignments from criminal networks operating mainly through social media. He used to take photographs of various locations and send them to his handler in return for money. He was paid in cryptocurrency and using GPay. The case bears some similarities to the Ebin Paul case, in which an incendiary device was thrown at the synagogue in Kochi. We are examining whether the handler is connected to that case,” Mr. Chandrasekhar told reporters.

Another youth was arrested in Mumbai recently for alleged links with Gurumurthy. Yash Singh, 20, a native of Navi Mumbai, was arrested by the Maharashtra Anti-Terrorism Squad for allegedly conducting reconnaissance of Jewish establishments, including Chabad House in Mumbai.
Mr. Singh, who was reportedly recruited by Gurumurthy, was later handed over to the Thrissur City police. He was brought to Thrissur on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody.

articles.title: Supreme Court asks Centre, States to file status reports on setting up of special courts to hear NDPS Act cases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Supreme Court took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts

The Supreme Court on Monday (November 16, 2026) asked the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to file fresh status reports on progress made in the establishment of 449 special courts to hear cases of heinous offences under the NDPS Act.

A Bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took note of the submissions of Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that not much progress has been made in pursuance of the orders passed by the apex court recently on setting up of special courts.
"This is a three-judge matter also," Justice Bagchi said and referred to the non-availability of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant for the hearing.

The Bench said that it will keep the suo motu case concerning the creation of exclusive special courts for speedy trials under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act after a few weeks and preferably before the winter vacation in December.
It asked the Centre, States and Union Territories to file fresh status reports on the progress made by them in creating special courts for early disposal of pending cases under the NIA and NDPS Acts.
Earlier, the Bench had expressed concern over the alarming increase in narcotics-related offences across the country and the growing pendency of cases under the NDPS Act.
On September 7, the court had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to expedite the establishment of exclusive special courts, preferably within six weeks.
According to an affidavit filed by the Union government, 449 exclusive NDPS courts have been identified as necessary across the country to address the mounting backlog of cases.
The Centre had told the court that 176 of these courts were already operational.

Taking note of the figures, the Bench had observed that the existing pendency and the "unfortunate, alarming increase" in offences under the NDPS Act made it imperative to establish all the identified courts at the earliest.

The Bench had directed the Centre, State governments and Union Territory administrations to ensure the necessary infrastructure and appointment of adequate staff so that the remaining courts could become operational preferably within six weeks.
Apart from NDPS cases, the Bench also reviewed the progress made by States in establishing exclusive special courts for trials under Section 11 of the NIA Act, 2008.
