articles.title: BJP seeks action against Italian political leader over remarks at Bharat Summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: BJP Telangana president Ramchander Rao claimed that Giacomo Filibeck, associated with the Party of European Socialists (PES), echoed slogans and criticisms directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the summit platform

The Telangana unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday (November 16, 2026) urged the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) to initiate action against Italian political leader Giacomo Filibeck and the organisers of the Bharat Summit, alleging that remarks made at the event violated Indian visa regulations and amounted to “interference in the country’s internal political affairs”.

A BJP delegation led by the State president N. Ramchander Rao submitted a complaint to the FRRO office at Shamshabad, seeking investigation into statements made by foreign representatives during the Congress-organised summit held in Hyderabad, and charging that the remarks targeted India’s democratic system and the Central government.

Addressing the media after submitting the complaint, Mr. Rao claimed that Mr. Filibeck, associated with the Party of European Socialists (PES), had echoed slogans and criticisms directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the summit platform. He argued that foreign nationals are not permitted to engage in political activities or comment on the host country’s internal political matters while visiting India.

The BJP leader cited provisions of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, and claimed that foreigners engaging in activities considered unlawful under the Act could face penal consequences. He demanded immediate action against Mr. Filibeck, including deportation and blacklisting if found to have violated visa norms.

Mr. Rao also called for criminal cases against the Bharat Summit organisers, alleging that the event, presented as a platform for discussion and investment, was used to promote an “anti-government narrative”. He further sought a detailed probe into the participation of both foreign and domestic delegates at the conclave.

The party’s State president said the BJP viewed the remarks as an affront to India’s democratic institutions and questioned the presence of senior Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy, during the event.

The party would also submit a complaint to the Director General of Police (DGP) and pursue the matter until legal action is taken, he added. General secretary Veerender Goud, chief spokesperson N.V. Subhash and others were present

articles.title: Wholesale inflation rises to 12.3% in October 2026, second straight month of double-digit inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: According to economists, not only will this high wholesale inflation soon translate into higher consumer prices, but it also means an interest rate hike is nearly certain, which would dampen economic sentiment

Wholesale inflation in India surged to 12.3% in October 2026, the second consecutive month of double-digit inflation, official data released on Monday (November 16, 2026) showed. Fuel prices continue to be the main reason for the price rise, with the crude petroleum and natural gas sectors seeing inflation of more than 70%.

The new series of the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry has data that goes back to only April 2024 and so a historical analysis for a longer duration is not possible. However, the data shows that inflation in October was the highest since at least then.
This data follows the release of Consumer Price Index data last week that showed that even retail inflation had climbed above the Reserve Bank of India’s upper comfort mark of 6% in October 2026.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, it is only a matter of time before wholesale inflation translates into a further increase in the prices consumers pay.

“It has been seen that manufactured goods in particular have witnessed an increase of 9.5%, with high inflation rates in textiles, tobacco products, chemicals, rubber products, metals and electrical equipment,” Mr. Sabnavis pointed out. “This will pressurise companies into increasing their product prices at some point of time.”
“This passthrough will get reflected in the core part of the CPI in the coming months depending on the actions of industry,” he added.

Further, as Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive argues, the high WPI inflation makes a rate hike by the RBI in December a near certainty, which would have a further dampening effect on the economy.

“The sharp rise in WPI inflation to 12.39% in October 2026 reinforces the inflationary concerns already reflected in elevated retail inflation readings,” Payal V. Pandya, vice president at Bajaj Broking Prive said. “As a result, a rate hike by the RBI in the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting [in December] now looks almost certain.”

“Higher interest rates may impact lending activity, investments, and consumption, while sentiment across the financial sector could remain under pressure,” Ms. Pandya added. “With geopolitical tensions resurfacing in the Russia-Ukraine region, risks to inflation and economic growth have become even more pronounced.”

Within the WPI, food inflation climbed to 8.3% in October 2026, the highest in 22 months. The overall fuel and power category saw inflation jump to nearly 33% in the same month, compared to about 26% in September 2026. These high levels were, however, also a result of a low base, since this segment of the WPI was in contraction for large parts of 2025.
Similarly, the crude petroleum and natural gas segment saw inflation climb to 70.8% in October 2026 from 57.3% in September. This was compared to a 7.2% contraction in prices in October of last year.

articles.title: Iron ore capacity under-utilisation in major-producing states prompt concerns as India sets 2047 target
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With India’s iron ore demand projected to rise to 772 million tonnes (MT) by 2047, miners in Odisha, the country’s largest iron ore reserve holder, are yet to utilise nearly 40% of their existing capacities, raising concerns over resource wastage and potential revenue losses.
The issue has come under judicial scrutiny, with both the Supreme Court earlier this month and the Odisha High Court in January flagging the underutilisation of mining capacities.

The Odisha High Court, while agreeing with petitioners who highlighted the sluggish operationalisation of mines despite environmental clearances, observed that the delay had resulted in an average annual revenue loss of ₹4,000 crore to the State.
However, industry sources, speaking on condition of anonymity, attributed the delays primarily to prolonged forest clearance procedures, which often exceed the stipulated 18-month timeframe.

Data cited by petitioner Citizens’ Action Forum (Bhubaneswar) show that of the 246 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) of mining capacity granted environmental clearance in FY25, only around 159 MTPA had been operationalised.

Separately, data published by mining consultancy BigMint in June 2026 show that Odisha produced 158 MT of iron ore in FY26 against an environmentally cleared capacity of 278 MTPA, indicating capacity utilisation of nearly 60%.
The underutilised capacity is particularly significant as it largely involves hematite, which is among the highest-grade varieties of iron ore

The shortfall also raises questions over India’s continued dependence on imports. According to the Mines Ministry, the country imported 12.3 MT of iron ore in FY26, incurring an expenditure of ₹11,115 crore.

Odisha accounted for more than 50% of India’s domestic iron ore production during FY26. Chhattisgarh contributed around 17.1%, followed by Karnataka at 16.6%. Capacity utilisation in the two states – albeit with significantly lower volumes than Odisha – stood at 62% and 80%, respectively, according to calculations based on BigMint data.

In January, the Odisha High Court directed that mining rights be mandatorily transferred to state-owned National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) to ensure “optimum utilisation of the mines” and “eradicate any burden on the government exchequer”.

However, in its November 4 order, the Supreme Court concurred with the need for optimum utilisation of mineral resources but left the decision on transferring mining rights to the State government’s discretion, rather than making it mandatory.

articles.title: COP31 draft deal calls for ‘accelerated action’ to exit fossil fuels
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: COP31 co-host Australia released the first draft of a broad political deal on Monday (November 16, 2026) that includes a call for nations to speed up the phaseout of planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
The draft decision needs ultimate approval by nearly 200 nations at the UN climate summit in Turkiye where the future of fossil fuels has been among the most heated issues.
The proposed agreement lays out the competing positions of governments in Antalya and underscores how far apart they remain with a consensus deal due by Friday.
The draft "calls for accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels, including through the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems".

It also evokes "deep concern" over the impending breach of the Paris accord's 1.5C target and recognises the "central role of the best-available science" of the IPCC, the global authority on climate change.
Many countries, particularly in Europe and climate-vulnerable developing nations, have pushed for a reference to the IPCC and urged a faster exit from fossil fuels in the final text.
The text also calls for a "tripling" of finance for climate adaptation measures in developing countries to reach at least $120 billion, a key demand of these nations.
Australia, which is steering the marathon talks, wants to produce an overarching political statement summing up what countries have agreed in Antalya and setting the course for future climate action.
The summit, which closes on November 20, takes place against a difficult backdrop, with a conflict-driven energy crisis and geopolitical tensions tempering expectations.

articles.title: Italian political leader’s speech in India draws criticism in his own country
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Deborah Bergamini said Europeans should not give lessons on democracy to India, which has 970 million voters.

An Italian political leader's remarks criticising the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during a recent event in India have drawn criticism in his country, with a senior leader of the ruling coalition in Rome saying it is “inappropriate” to intervene in a friendly nation's internal political debate.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), Mr. Filibeck had expressed support for Indian opposition leader Rahul Gandhi's campaign against alleged irregularities in the country’s electoral rolls and used the slogan "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod," a Hindi political slogan that translates as “Those who stole the vote must vacate their seats”.

VIDEO | Hyderabad: At the Bharat Summit, Secretary General of the Party of European Socialists, Giacomo Filibeck said, "Rahul Gandhi has defended a simple principle on which every democracy rests; 'one person, one vote'. articles.title: Beijing hails ‘groundbreaking significance’ of U.S., China, Russia summit in Shenzhen
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control

Thursday’s (November 19, 2026) summit meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia will be “of groundbreaking significance”, Beijing said on Monday (November 16, 2026), hailing the symbolism of a meeting of the three leaders taking place in China.
China’s Foreign Ministry said President Xi Jinping will host the summit with President Donald Trump and President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit.

“The upcoming China-Russia-U.S. summit in Shenzhen will mark the first-ever face-to-face meeting among the heads of state of the three countries. The three leaders will exchange views in depth on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-country relations, and the meeting will be of groundbreaking significance,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said, adding that “strengthening communication, managing differences and stabilising relations among China, Russia and the U.S. serve the interests of all three countries”.

The meeting is likely to be more symbolic than substantial. U.S. officials have indicated that the agenda is the war in Ukraine, the situation in West Asia, including stabilising global energy supplies, and nuclear arms control. Whether there will be any concrete outcomes on any of those issues remains to be seen.

That has not, however, dampened enthusiasm in China, where state media has hailed the significance of the meeting. Beijing officially eschews references to a “G2” with the U.S. or a “G3” with the two countries and Russia, maintaining that it supports multipolarity. At the same time, the symbolism of China hosting the meeting has been seized upon to highlight Beijing’s global standing.

“The fact that China, Russia and the U.S. will sit down for face-to-face talks once again demonstrates that the head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance,” an editorial in the Global Times said. “The effort to foster a new type of major-country relationship marks a new phase in China’s major-country diplomacy with Chinese characteristics, featured by proactive leadership and systematic construction. The meeting to be held in Shenzhen is a manifestation of the international community’s high recognition of China’s image as a stable and responsible major country.”

Taking aim at naysayers, the editorial added that “those who view the trilateral meeting between China, Russia and the U.S. as major countries ‘carving out new spheres of influence’ or establishing a ‘new Yalta system’ clearly hold only a one-sided view of history, ignoring historical patterns.”

“They focus solely on the needs of individual parties while disregarding the overall and comprehensive interests, emphasise only the power aspect of major countries while neglecting their responsibilities, and are so preoccupied with the reality of polarisation in the international landscape that they lose sight of the ideal of democratising international relations,” it said.

Symbolism aside, few experts in China expect substantial outcomes amid what they acknowledge is growing strategic rivalry between China and the U.S. on the one hand, and an enduring rift between Russia and the West on the other, especially with the continuing war in Ukraine. Russia was “most enthusiastic” among the three for the summit, Su Liuqiang, a scholar at the Centre for American Studies at the Shanghai Institutes for International Studies, said in an interview with state media last week, adding that an informal exchange was likelier than a more structured, formal trilateral summit.

“On the one hand, there is substantial political resistance in the U.S.,” he said. “Anti-Russia sentiment remains strong in both the U.S. and among its European allies, with opposition to negotiating with Moscow while bypassing Ukraine and Europe. On the other hand, the three countries have differing priorities; Russia’s core concern is negotiations on a ceasefire in Ukraine, the U.S. is interested in the Russia-Ukraine conflict and non-proliferation, China supports peace talks but must also balance its relations with the U.S., Russia, Europe and Ukraine. In this context, a low-profile trilateral meeting is the more realistic option,” he added, noting that practical outcomes could emphasise stabilising global energy supplies.

While China preferred “multilateralism” over ideas such as the G2 or a U.S.-China-Russia triumvirate, Mr. Su said a meeting would still be significant in suggesting that while structural competition between big powers would still continue to define global geopolitics, there was increasing interest in “managing that competition and preventing it from escalating or spinning out of control.”

articles.title: EU accuses Russia of stalling Ukraine peace talks to target power plants as winter nears
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: At talks in Brussels, EU foreign ministers said the priority should be to secure a ceasefire and then a real peace agreement

European Union countries on Monday (November 16, 2026) accused Russia of trying to drag out talks on ending the war in Ukraine while it bombs power plants and other infrastructure to make life even harder for civilians as winter closes in.

At talks in Brussels, EU foreign ministers said the priority should be to secure a ceasefire and then a real peace agreement. They said that Russia started the nearly five-year war and must back down rather than make fresh demands of Ukraine and its Western backers.

"Let's not blur the picture right now. What we need to see is a ceasefire," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said before chairing the meeting. "We don't see it at the moment. We see that Russia is really escalating."

After negotiations in Abu Dhabi last week, the United States encouraged Ukraine and its backers to agree to a Russian demand for a new security framework for Europe, suggesting that it might help bring peace.
European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas rings a bell to signify the start of a meeting of EU foreign ministers at the European Council building in Brussels, on November 16 | Photo Credit: AP

But the Europeans see that as a Russian attempt to weaken NATO by obliging the military alliance to pull troops and equipment back westward, similar to the way they were deployed before the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland joined in 1999.

That demand is "really absurd", Ms. Kallas said. "If we look at the history, none of these countries has ever attacked Russia." She said Russia's tactic is always to demand more even though "they started the war. They are the aggressor. And there's one victim".

Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee, whose country currently holds the EU's rotating presidency, said that despite the talks, “Russia has clearly not changed its position. It is continuing its attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure."

Ms. McEntee said the EU will agree on more sanctions later Monday, "trying to in particular attack the financial mechanism by which Russia is waging this war". The ministers will also look at ways to help Ukraine endure the coming winter.

German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said, "Europe has a security architecture — we don't need a new one, we just need respect from everyone for the existing security architecture." He said that is "the foundation for any conceivable agreement, from the European point of view".
Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys also insisted that Europe does not need another security framework, saying Russia cannot be trusted and has already broken past agreements anyway.

"It's very clear that we don't need another one. We already have one. Secure Ukraine, strong Europe, strong trans-Atlantic bond," he told reporters. "It's not about the rules. Rules are working. The problem is that Russia is breaking them."

articles.title: French troops deployed in Ukraine on secret mission: RFI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026

French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine for several months, training Ukrainian troops and helping maintain military equipment, Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Citing sources, RFI said French lawmakers had not been informed of the deployment of the confidential mission, led by a French general and codenamed “Volia”, which can be translated as “freedom” and “will” from Ukrainian.
The report did not say how many soldiers took part in the mission, which has been present in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026.
It described a “light and flexible” structure made up of “small teams deployed on short-term assignments”.

Several sources described as being familiar with the matter told RFI that an official “Gerfaut” mission in Poland serves as a cover for the presence of French troops in Ukraine and acts as a gateway for deployments into the country.
Gerfaut is a French military detachment deployed in Poland since 2023 as part of the European Union’s military assistance mission supporting Ukraine.
Under that framework, French army personnel are tasked with training officers who will go on to command Ukrainian combat units.
Since 2023, 25,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been trained by the French army, both in France and in Poland.
France will hold a two-round vote in April and May to elect a successor to President Emmanuel Macron, who has been a staunch supporter of Ukraine.

The far-right National Rally (RN) party, whose leader, Marine Le Pen, is the frontrunner to replace Macron, has said that France would cut financial aid to Ukraine within six months if she is elected President.

articles.title: UN-backed talks consider possible rules on lethal autonomous weapons
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Scary would-be scenarios, like armed drones flying amok and gunning down civilians with pinpoint precision, have peppered years of discussions about killer robots, but those talks haven't produced any international restrictions

Killer robots and drones come up for a reckoning this week as Government envoys rev up a discussion and could decide whether to launch negotiations toward setting rules for the use of the deadly machines, or not.

Pope Leo XIV, the UN chief and advocacy groups cast the issue as an existential debate: Whether robots can be allowed to kill and whether humans must maintain some control of and accountability for the use of lethal autonomous weapon systems.

Activists say armed drones that can independently strike targets have already been deployed in some select instances in conflict zones like Ukraine and West Asia, but widespread rollout hasn't happened.

Scary would-be scenarios, like armed drones flying amok and gunning down civilians with pinpoint precision, have peppered years of discussions about killer robots. But those talks haven't produced any international restrictions.

The United States and Russia, longtime rivals, want to limit any curbs on their abilities to develop and roll out powerful new tools for the high-tech arms race, just as AI is gaining steam and changing battle plans.

The issue comes to a head at UN offices in Geneva, where a 7th review conference about the awkwardly named Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons will consider whether to start talks on regulation of killer robots.
Supporters of an accord acknowledge powerful forces are in the way, but point to precedent: Governments have already struck a deal to regulate blinding lasers.

Most countries support reining them in. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres' deadline this year for the launch of talks toward regulation has given the issue urgency, but some top military powers are hesitant.

Last month, seven countries, Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand, and Panama, submitted a proposal to launch negotiations of a new legally binding agreement on autonomous weapons at the conference.
The various sides have been gearing up for the diplomatic standoff.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), International Committee of the Red Cross president Mirjana Spoljaric said in a statement: “States must act to ensure the future of warfare is not handed over to machines.”
Stop Killer Robots, an advocacy group, says 130 countries support new international rules on the weapons systems.

articles.title: India scrutinises Red Bull’s sugar levels as ‘energy drink’ dispute escalates
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation, the FSSAI said in the document

India is scrutinising the composition of Red Bull, the drink made by the eponymous Austrian company, warning the product’s “energy drink” label could encourage people to consume too much added sugar, an official notice showed, opening a new front in the regulator’s fight over food safety standards.

It is the first time India has raised health concerns and questioned companies on the ingredients of their energy drinks in a dispute that began in June and has triggered legal challenges in the Delhi High Court.

In a confidential notice to Red Bull on Monday, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) targeted the drink’s “nutritional composition”, saying it derived a significant proportion of its declared energy from the “substantial” amount of added sugar.
“The basis and nature of the energy-related positioning of the product require scientific and regulatory substantiation,” the FSSAI said in the document, which was reviewed by Reuters.

The notice gives Red Bull seven days to explain why India should not prohibit its use of the “energy drink” label given it had the “potential to mislead consumers and encourage excessive consumption of added sugar.”
Red Bull and the FSSAI did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

India’s energy drinks market is set to be worth $1.6 billion by 2028, with sales growing 12.6% annually, faster than in the US and China, according to Euromonitor. Red Bull’s India revenue stood at $130 million in 2024, more than double the earnings recorded four years ago.

Health experts are concerned energy drinks contain high levels of sugar, caffeine and taurine, an amino acid that research suggests can contribute to health problems. The drinks will be banned for under-16s in England from April next year.

In court in recent weeks, Red Bull, PepsiCo, Monster Beverage and Reliance Consumer have challenged the June order banning the label “energy drinks”, saying they were not given any advance notice of the strict action.

However, while Red Bull managed to secure a temporary court injunction to enable it to continue using the “energy drink” label, its competitors were told that once they sold their existing stock they had to stop using the label.

The regulator has asked the Delhi judge to review the Red Bull decision because it says it gives the company “an undue commercial advantage” against its rivals, according to its October court filing reviewed by Reuters. That challenge will be heard in January.

In its latest notice, the FSSAI said Red Bull’s beverage carried a consumption advisory indicating the product should not be consumed in quantities exceeding 500 millilitres a day, which it said could confuse consumers into believing it was fine to consume that quantity.

articles.title: Study provides atlas of links between early-life environmental exposures, health
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The authors "identified a set of 'master regulator' exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence"

Environmental exposures during pregnancy and childhood, including tobacco smoke, indoor air pollution and dietary quality, may be associated with health outcomes such as BMI and behaviour, with many of these links persisting into adolescence, a new study has found.

Researchers, led by those at the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal), identified six prenatal and 42 childhood exposures associated with multiple outcomes and health families simultaneously.

The study, published in Science Advances , provides an atlas of associations between early-life environmental exposures and health, highlighting factors that may be relevant for prevention and policy action.

"Our approach allowed us to jointly analyse associations between the early-life exposome and multiple health outcomes instead of studying each one separately," first author Augusto Anguita-Ruiz, ISGlobal and University of Barcelona researcher, said.
The researchers used an outcome-wide exposome approach to study associations of exposures with health across four domains -- cardiometabolic, mental health, respiratory, and allergic problems.
The exposome refers to the totality of environmental exposures a person experiences throughout life, including factors such as diet, tobacco smoke and air pollution.

The exposures examined included diet, physical activity, sleep and other individual behaviours, as well as tobacco smoke, indoor and outdoor air pollution, chemical pollutants, metals and characteristics of the built environment.

The authors "identified a set of 'master regulator' exposures, such as maternal smoking, indoor air pollution, endocrine-disrupting chemicals, and dietary and urban factors, that influenced multiple health domains, with effects persisting into adolescence."

Senior co-author Valérie Siroux, researcher at the French National Institute for Health and Medical Research (Inserm), said: "Although no exposure was associated with all four domains, around one in three of the selected exposures was linked to more than one, suggesting that certain exposures can have broad and multisystemic effects on health."

Maternal smoking during pregnancy was associated with higher BMI and more externalising behaviours, such as aggression and impulsivity, in children during both early childhood and adolescence, as well as more ADHD symptoms during adolescence.
Higher maternal meat intake during pregnancy was also associated with several mental health outcomes and asthma in children, as well as wheezing and dermatitis during childhood.
Associations between environmental exposures and health parameters observed in early childhood were found to persist in adolescence.

articles.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Only 42 countries -- less than one in five -- had a national action plan on AMR that was financed, implemented and monitored, according to the World Health Organization

The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday, November 16, 2026.
WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets.
Bacteria have long evolved resistance to medicines designed to kill them.
The widespread use of antibiotics in human health, animal husbandry and food production has accelerated the problem, making AMR one of the leading causes of infectious-disease deaths worldwide.

"Antimicrobial resistance is widespread and threatening the future of modern medicine," said Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, interim head of antimicrobial resistance at the WHO. "Unlike COVID-19, which was very visible, drug-resistant infections have been taking people's lives for years without us noticing it and raising the alarm as we should," said Nyemazi.
In 2021 alone, AMR was directly responsible for more than one million deaths and linked to some 4.7 million others, said the agency.

A WHO investigation in 183 countries into the progress of the fight against antimicrobial resistance this year revealed that nearly nine countries in 10 had a national action plan against the phenomenon. In 2017, the figure was only around four in 10.
But only 42 countries -- less than one in five -- said they had a plan that was financed, implemented and monitored, said Pravasha Prakash, an AMR technical officer with the global health agency.
"Countries are moving forward in every step but progress still needs to be speeded up to reach the 2030 targets," she added.

One of the main weaknesses remains access to diagnostics. Only 36% of countries had a national reference laboratory capable of testing for resistance in all bacteria and fungi monitored by the WHO -- well short of the 80% target set for 2030.
"Without testing, clinicians must treat without knowing the cause of infection or which antibiotic will work," said Sylvia Bertagnolo, head of surveillance for AMR at the WHO.
The latest global surveillance data show that in 2023, one in every six laboratory-confirmed bacterial infections flagged to the WHO was resistant to antibiotics used to treat it.

articles.title: IIT-Madras launches heart health awareness campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Hridayam is a social campaign to raise awareness about cardiovascular health and prevention among young people

Shaastra 2027, the annual techno-managerial festival of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Madras, has launched Hridayam, a social campaign to raise awareness about cardiovascular health and prevention among young people.

The initiative, in collaboration with Cardiac Wellness Institute, began with a session on stress management for students, led by Priya Chockalingam, clinical director of the institute. The session covered the effects of acute and chronic stress on heart health and practical approaches to managing stress. A pre-session assessment found that academic workload, extracurricular activities, and job placement concerns were major sources of stress among students.

Students also visited the institute to interact with patients undergoing cardiac rehabilitation and learn about the role of diet, physical activity, sleep and stress management in maintaining heart health. The campaign will conclude during Shaastra, scheduled from January 2 to 6, 2027, with heart health screenings for visitors.

articles.title: Jordan blocks Telegram app over national security concerns

fullParagraphs: The decision comes after a ⁠rare deadly church attack last month killed nine people and prompted airstrikes on neighbouring Syria that ​Jordan said ‌killed 20 Islamic State militants
Jordanian ​authorities said on Monday that they will ‌block the Telegram social media app ​in the kingdom over national ⁠security concerns.

Jordan's Public Security Directorate said its approach aimed to safeguard society against threats ‌including "attempts to spread extremism and radicalisation — all of which threaten societal security ‌and national interests — in accordance ‌with existing ⁠legislation."

The decision comes after a ⁠rare deadly church attack last month killed nine people and prompted airstrikes on neighbouring Syria that ​Jordan said ‌killed 20 Islamic State militants. The three assailants were sentenced to death on Sunday.
On November 5, Jordan said ‌that one security officer had been ​killed and another wounded in what it called a terrorist stabbing ⁠attack in Amman.
Over the years, Islamic State militants have used the mobile messaging ‌service, created by Pavel Durov, who is in exile from Russia, to issue statements.
Telegram did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

Durov faces investigations in several countries. ‌In July, Russia said it had charged him ​with facilitating terrorist activity, alleging that his app was being used ⁠by Ukrainian spies to organise attacks inside Russia.
Durov ⁠denies wrongdoing and says Telegram has exceeded its obligations to ‌moderate content and cooperate with authorities to fight crime.

articles.title: UK regulator orders tougher action on child abuse material ahead of next year's social media ban
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: It will ​also require them ‌to expand the use of technology to detect and remove known illegal images, and in some cases, deploy ‌automated tools to identify previously ​unknown content

Britain's media regulator Ofcom on Monday ​tightened online child-safety rules , requiring platforms to ‌take stronger action against child ​sexual abuse material and grooming ⁠ahead of a planned ban on social media access for under-16s.

The new duties, which ‌Ofcom expects to take effect from early 2027 subject to parliamentary ‌approval, will require social media ‌platforms, ⁠file-sharing services, pornography sites and other ⁠online services to ban users who generate, upload or share child sexual abuse material.
It will ​also require them ‌to expand the use of technology to detect and remove known illegal images, and in some cases, deploy ‌automated tools to identify previously ​unknown content.
Britain announced in June its plan to ban ⁠under-16s from accessing social media platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat and X, saying ‌the measures would help "give kids their childhood back."
Ofcom said the new measures announced on Monday were needed because of the scale of child sexual abuse material online, which it said ‌had been exacerbated by advances in ​artificial intelligence.

"While we have seen progress from industry on tackling child sexual ⁠abuse on their platforms, we are ⁠not satisfied that enough is being done," said Oliver Griffiths, director ‌of Ofcom's Online Safety Group.

articles.title: Kumara Krupa Guest House now turned into Chief Minister’s official residence, renamed ‘Ganga’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Chief Minister says chose to relocate to the Kumara Krupa Guest House as the quarters sanctioned to him were small, and as the Kumara Krupa Guest House was not being used

The old Kumara Krupa Guest House in Bengaluru has now been converted into the Chief Minister’s official residence and has been renamed “Ganga”. In a private ceremony on Monday, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar performed puja at the new residence and also announced that all the legislators and MPs will be invited on Thursday to the new residence.
The Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms (DPAR) issued a notification on Monday, renaming the old guest house “Ganga” and declaring it as the Chief Minister’s official residence.
The Chief Minister said he had chosen to relocate to the Kumara Krupa Guest House as the quarters sanctioned to him were small and the Kumara Krupa Guest House was not being used.
A view of Kumara Krupa Guest House in Bengaluru. | Photo Credit: File Photo

The Chief Minister said the old building had been slightly renovated without altering its heritage value, denying allegations to the contrary. He maintained that Opposition leaders would be able to verify the same when he invites them to the programme on Thursday.

Referring to the curiosity and concerns regarding the cost of renovation, he said efforts had been made to minimise the cost, including using inexpensive marble and Kota stone for the flooring. Old furniture from the guest house had been used, while furniture from his own house too had been brought to avoid buying new furniture, he explained. To a query on the total cost of the renovation, the Chief Minister said he was yet to receive the bill.

He said his family would shift to the new residence in about eight days. However, he would start meeting leaders at this residence starting Thursday. A separate hall was being built for meeting officials and the general public. However, it was expected to take another two months to complete the proposed structure, he noted.

Defending the decision to turn the heritage building into his official residence, Mr. Shivakumar said, “None of us is permanent here. The building has been renovated to ensure that it will serve as the official residence for all those who become Chief Ministers.”

articles.title: ‘I Love Hussain Sagar Lake’ campaign launched to promote conservation and tourism
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Vasavi Club Buddhapurnima, affiliated to Vasavi Clubs International, has launched the ‘I Love Hussain Sagar Lake’ campaign, calling upon citizens to take collective responsibility for protecting one of Hyderabad’s most iconic landmarks.

The campaign was launched at a programme held aboard the Khair-un-Nissa boat on Hussainsagar over the weekend. N. Manvi Jagan, deputy general manager of the Telangana Tourism Development Corporation (TGTDC), unveiled a series of campaign posters highlighting the need to protect the lake, prevent pollution and promote its tourism potential.

The posters carried messages such as ‘Hyderabad Is Incomplete Without Hussain Sagar’, ‘More Than a Lake. It’s Hyderabad’s Identity’, ‘Hussain Sagar Lake Is Not a Dustbin’, ‘A Clean Hussain Sagar Is Everyone’s Responsibility’ and ‘Make Hussain Sagar a Tourist’s Delight’. The campaign also urged visitors to avoid plastic, protect the lake’s heritage and become ambassadors for its conservation.

D. Ramchandram, project coordinator of the campaign and co-chairman of the tourism committee of Federation of Telangana Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FTCCI), pointed out that lakes and waterfronts across the world have evolved into major tourism destinations, offering boating, cruising, sailing, water sports, heritage experiences and leisure activities.

V.N. Telukuntla Venkat Raghuram, president of Vasavi Club Buddhapurnima, said Hussainsagar is an invaluable part of Hyderabad’s heritage and identity and that its protection cannot be left to the government alone. Every citizen has a responsibility towards preserving the lake for future generations, he said.

articles.title: One in five northeast women deficient in vitamin B1: ICMR-NIN study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Around one in five pregnant and lactating women in Assam’s Barak Valley and adjoining districts of Tripura suffer from suboptimal levels of ‘Thiamine’ (vitamin B1), according to a study by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN), Hyderabad, highlighting a continuing public health concern in the region.

The study, ‘Re-Emergence of Thiamine Deficiency Among Pregnant and Lactating Women in Northeast India’, published in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, examined the prevalence of thiamine deficiency and its link to dietary practices in areas where beriberi cases have previously been reported, said a press release on Monday.

Researchers conducted the community-based study during 2023-24 among 1,083 women from 120 villages in Assam’s Barak Valley and neighbouring parts of Tripura. Thiamine status was assessed using biochemical and functional indicators to determine the extent of deficiency.

The findings showed that about 20% of participants had inadequate thiamine levels. Based on blood thiamine measurements, 4.9% were deficient, and 15.2% had marginal levels. A separate functional assessment produced similar results, with 8.5% showing severe deficiency and 12.1% marginal deficiency. Pregnant women were found to be more vulnerable than lactating mothers.

Thiamine is an essential micronutrient that supports energy metabolism and healthy nervous system function. Deficiency can lead to serious health complications, making adequate intake particularly important during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

According to Mahesh Kumar Mummadi, NIN scientist and lead author of the study, dietary assessments revealed that most women consumed rice-based diets with limited diversity. Practices such as consuming stored rice, repeatedly washing rice before cooking, chewing betel nut and drinking salted tea were associated with a higher risk of deficiency.

NIN director Bharati Kulkarni said the findings underscore the need to look beyond routinely monitored nutrients in maternal health programmes. She called for greater dietary diversity, regular nutritional surveillance and targeted supplementation in high-risk regions. Researchers also noted that since the study focused on areas with previously reported beriberi clusters, the findings may not be representative of all pregnant and lactating women across India.

articles.title: Rights panel orders probe into boy’s electrocution in Keralam’s Malappuram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Commission judicial member K. Baijunath directed the Malappuram District Collector and the KSEB executive engineer to investigate the cause of the accident and submit a report within 15 days.

The State Human Rights Commission has registered a case and ordered an inquiry into the death of 14-year-old Junaid, who was electrocuted by a stay wire attached to an electric post at Cherumukku near Tirurangadi in the district on Sunday (November 15).

Commission judicial member K. Baijunath directed the Malappuram District Collector and the KSEB executive engineer to investigate the cause of the accident and submit a report within 15 days. The case will be considered at a sitting of the Commission in Tirur on December 3.

The incident has triggered protests, with residents alleging negligence by the KSEB. Residents who gathered at the accident site questioned officials over their failure to address the danger, claiming that the stay wire had remained in a hazardous condition for nearly three years. They also alleged that several other stay wires in the area posed similar risks.

KSEB officials who visited the site were surrounded and detained by protesters, leading to heated arguments. Following the protest, senior KSEB officials gave a written assurance that action would be taken against those found responsible.
Junaid’s father Shihab E. and uncle Ismail Darimi said they lost the child due to negligence on the part of the KSEB authorities.
Three other children were with Junaid when the accident occurred. They escaped because they were on a tractor and the driver intervened in time.
Junaid’s body was buried at the Cherumukku Juma Masjid cemetery.

Power Minister Sunny Joseph ordered an investigation and sought a report from the KSEB deputy chief engineer at Tirurangadi. The investigation will examine whether officials failed to act on earlier complaints about the hazardous stay wire and whether there was any delay in addressing the risk.

The Minister directed officials to remove electricity lines that had remained unused and unrepaired for more than a year. He also ordered the KSEB to provide appropriate compensation to Junaid’s family.

The KSEB, meanwhile, publicly apologised to Junaid’s family and the public, admitting that the incident should never have happened. It has promised an impartial inquiry and stricter inspection of electricity lines across the State.
Th KSEB urged the public to report electricity-related safety hazards by sending photographs and details via WhatsApp to 94960-10101.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi unveils her memoir Belonging - A Journey of Love with Rahul, Priyanka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Response to the book has been overwhelming, I’m deeply touched,” said Sonia Gandhi during the book launch event
Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi formally launched her memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , with Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi by her side on Monday (November 16, 2026).
“Response to the book has been overwhelming, I’m deeply touched,” said Sonia Gandhi during the book launch event.
‘Belonging’ means ‘you belong’; when you’re an outsider, you feel not being liked & always watched, Sonia Gandhi added on the book title.

Several INDIA bloc leaders, including Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC’s Abhishek Banerjee, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay and BJP leader Amarinder Singh attended the launch of Sonia Gandhi’s memoir on Monday (November 16, 2026).

Published by HarperCollins India, Belonging: A Journey of Love was released last Tuesday (November 10, 2026) to a lot of enthusiasm from readers, who have been lining up at prominent bookstores to pick up copies of the memoir while many have been ordering it online.
Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chief Rahul Gandhi and AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were present at the official launch event at the ITC Maurya.

Other than Mr. Vijay, Akhilesh Yadav and Mr. Banerjee, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren, J&K Chief Minister Omar Obdullah, National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule, BJP leader and ex-Punjab Chief Minister Amarinder Singh, Congress chief ministers D. K. Shivakumar (Karnataka) and Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu (Himachal Pradesh) also attended the launch event, along with several senior Congress leaders.

VIDEO | Delhi: Explaining why she decided to write her memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi says much has been written about her family, including her mother-in-law, husband, son, daughter and herself, but most of it is far removed from reality. "Stories are woven around you. Untruths are woven around you, hurtful things are said which are nowhere near the truth. And I thought, well, perhaps this is a way of bringing out my feelings, what I know of my family, and maybe people will be sort of open to listen to my story too," she said.

articles.title: Amid drought, vegetable prices soar in Yadgir
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Drumstick breaches ₹200 per kg mark, while onion climbs to ₹70 a kg

People in Yadgir district who suffered a severe drought and also, a hike in the prices of essential commodities earlier this year are now facing the brunt of skyrocketing vegetable prices in the retail market.
Deficit rainfall and depletion in the groundwater levels have considerably hit local horticultural production, affecting the pockets of consumers.
According to sources in the retail market, drumstick, a staple for wedding ceremonies and other auspicious functions, has emerged as the costliest vegetable, selling at over ₹200 a kg.
Carrot, cluster beans, bitter gourd and capsicum are retailing at ₹80 a kg, while green chilli, lady’s finger (okra), beetroot and cauliflower are priced at ₹60 a kg.
Amid the steep hike across the board, tomato offers a slight respite to shoppers, selling between ₹25 a kg and ₹30 a kg.

The sharp rise in the price of onion, an indispensable ingredient in everyday vegetarian and non-vegetarian cooking, to ₹70 a kg has left middle-class families in both urban and rural pockets distressed.

“We normally use onions in almost every dish. However, with prices surging, we are forced to ration them strictly for essential preparations and rely on garlic as a substitute for routine cooking,” homemaker Girija said.
Officials from the Agriculture Department attributed the price hike to the failure of the monsoon which has caused a steep drop in the watertable.

“A majority of borewells have dried up. Farmers who previously cultivated vegetables using pumpset water to irrigate them have now shifted focus towards rabi sowing. With the rabi rain also failing so far, local vegetable output has declined substantially,” an official said.
Currently, the district relies heavily on onion supplies transported from Maharashtra via Kalaburagi or other areas depending on availability.
Vegetable trader Moinuddin noted that delays in freight movement also have further pushed up retail costs.
“Regardless of the volume imported from neighbouring States, prices will stabilise only when local produce enters the market,” he observed.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.

“We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death,” she said ‌in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday (November 11, 2026).

Karnataka is set to host the 29th edition of its flagship annual technology exposition, the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS), from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC).
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will inaugurate the three-day event, themed: “AI & Beyond,” on Tuesday morning.

Addressing a media conference on the eve of the summit, Minister for Home, IT & BT, and e-Governance Priyank Kharge said that the conference would feature over 120 knowledge sessions across 16 thematic tracks, including IT & DeepTech, Frontier Tech, Electro-Semicon, Electric Mobility, Health & Biotech, Digital Infrastructure & Data Centres, Data & Cybersecurity, Assistive Tech, Focus GCC, Circular Economy, Orange Economy, Finverse, Skilling & Edutech, India–USA Tech Conclave, Global Collaborations, and India Innovates.

Highlighting the summit’s global trajectory, Mr. Kharge noted how the expo has expanded over the decades to draw international participation. “Bengaluru Tech Summit has evolved beyond an annual technology gathering into a platform where global conversations translate into partnerships, investments, and tangible opportunities,” the Minister said.
The State’s ambition was to make Bengaluru a gateway for the world to engage with India’s technology ecosystem, while taking Karnataka’s innovations and solutions to global markets, he added.

According to Mr. Kharge, the 2026 edition introduces several new initiatives, including the debut of the GCC India Leaders’ Dialogue on Wednesday and a new Workshops & Masterclass Series featuring 11 sessions by global firms such as Nvidia, Cloudflare, and eBay. The summit will also host three co-located international events: the maiden edition of Germany’s embedded world India, alongside France-origin sustainability and health forums ChangeNOW and One Sustainable Health.

A 50,000 sq. ft. AI & Robotics Pavilion co-curated by Bharat1.ai, showcasing indigenous humanoids, drones, and India’s first quadrupedal athletic showcase, would be a new feature. The summit will also mark the launch of AI Kavach, the country’s first AI cybersecurity lab for the BFSI (banking, financial services and insurance) sector developed with IIT Kanpur.

Backed by Karnataka’s Global Innovation Alliance, which has expanded from 10 countries in 2018 to over 40 nations, the event will have Sweden as its Country Partner, alongside delegations from over 65 countries. Over 1,000 startups from 100 Indian cities will participate, culminating on November 19 with the Future Makers Conclave to celebrate 10 years of Karnataka’s ELEVATE initiative and felicitate recent unicorns and IPO achievers.

articles.title: DVAC registers criminal case over alleged irregularities in the purchase of books
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The criminal case has been registered against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore. On Monday (November 16, 2026), DVAC officials launched a search at seven places and seized receipt vouchers for book procurement and other documents. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers, was arrested

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a criminal case against a Chennai-based publisher and “unidentified officials” of the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library, Chennai, and Periyar Arivulagam, Coimbatore, over allegations of large-scale irregularities in the procurement of books.

The case was registered after prima facie evidence pointing to forgery, criminal conspiracy, and corruption was established in a detailed inquiry conducted on a complaint filed by the Secretary, School Education Department, who sought a probe into the alleged irregularities in the procurement of books for public libraries.
Investigation revealed that the “coordination committee” had added titles not recommended by the “books recommendation committee”, which had proposed around 26,000 books for purchase.
These additions were not brought on record in the official note file, the First Information Report said.

It also revealed that books were allegedly written in fictitious names, with plagiarised content and violations of the Transparent Book Procurement Policy, 2024, which prescribed a systematic, transparent, and structured procedure for the purchase of books for public libraries.

Besides the officials, the agency booked R. Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers (also known as Akal Vilakku Pathippagam), and Phoenix Publications, both based at Madipakkam, Chennai, and other unidentified persons.

The DVAC said in its FIR that the State government had sanctioned ₹50 crore for procuring books and e-books for Periyar Arivulagam. The procurement was also intended to cover Kamarajar Arivulagam, Tiruchi; Bharathidasan Arivulagam, Salem; Anjalai Ammal Arivulagam, Cuddalore; Quaid-e-Millath Arivulagam, Tirunelveli; and libraries in six newly formed districts.

The agency said Mohan was the proprietor of both publishing firms that had operated from the same address and were associated with Sigma Prints and Sigma Publishing Services. He had given a list of 2,339 titles in the name of Akal Vizhakku Publishers and 99 titles in the name of Phoenix Publications. Purchase orders for 1,857 books were issued to the two publishers on February 13 and 14, 2026. After the books were received and verified, the list submitted by Akal Vizhakku Publishers was forwarded for processing payment for 1,779 books.

Investigators said Mohan had “created the books under fictitious author names, using information taken from websites and online applications, including ChatGPT. The contents were found to be vague, irrelevant and misleading, and of substandard language with no educational or informational value for a public library”.

The inquiry exposed instances of factually wrong information and plagiarism. One book described Naladiyar as a poet and philosopher, while another said the author of Madurai Kanchi was a king. The book titled Tourism: Principles, Practices and Philosophies, attributed to Emily Lawson, contained material copied from other books.

“The State government paid from public funds to the two publications for books which were written under false author names, in some cases copied from other works, and not fit for a public library,” the DVAC said.

The inquiry revealed that the procurement of books from Akal Vilakku Pathipagam and Phoenix Publications was done not only for Periyar Arivulagam but also for other public libraries at a cost of ₹1.74 crore. The investigation would be extended to unearth whether other publishers supplied similar books to the public libraries.

articles.title: Delhi car blast: SC allows transfer of cases to capital for joint trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed a plea by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) for transfer of two criminal cases linked to the November 2025 car explosion near the Red Fort Metro station from Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana to a special court in the national capital.
A Bench headed by Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra also directed that three FIRs registered in the matter across Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Haryana be clubbed together for a joint trial in Delhi.
A powerful explosion ripped through a slow-moving car at a traffic signal near the Red Fort Metro station on November 10, 2025, killing 12 people and injuring several others.

The apex court pointed to the overlapping of accused persons, witnesses and evidence, making separate trials in different States unfeasible. The court also took into consideration the security of the trial, with several accused persons still absconding.

The NIA said the cases were linked through an interweaving of facts, like the proliferation of provocative and inflammatory posters associated with the proscribed terrorist organisation Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) in Srinagar, ahead of the blast.
All three cases were intricately connected and formed part of one overarching conspiracy, requiring a joint trial in one place.
Following the blast, several arrests were made, including that of four doctors. The alleged car bomber, Umar Nabi, was reported to be a doctor himself.

articles.title: Charge sheet against six in conspiracy to raise funds for TRF: police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Mukhtar Ahmad Baba, a TRF-linked terrorist operating from Pakistan, used hawala and other covert channels to send funds into J&K, CIK stated

Counter Intelligence Kashmir (CIK), a special cell of the J&K Police, filed a charge sheet on Monday (November 16, 2026) against six people accused of a “conspiracy to raise and route funds to a banned outfit, The Resistance Front (TRF)” .
A CIK spokesman said the charge sheet was filed before the court of the Special Judge Designated Under NIA Act (TADA/POTA), Srinagar.

“Mukhtar Ahmad Baba, a TRF-linked terrorist operating from Pakistan, used hawala and other covert channels to send funds into J&K. Three Srinagar residents — Erfan Gul, Shazia Nazir, and Riyaz Ahmad Gojri — travelled to Saudi Arabia ostensibly for Umrah (pilgrimage). There they met Baba’s associates and received TRF funds to distribute among terrorists, separatists, and over-ground workers,” the CIK said.
The CIK claimed that digital devices containing key evidence were seized during searches. It said Gul, Nazir, and Gojri have been charged under BNS Sections 61(2), and 152, and UAPA Section 13.

The agency added that three other accused — Mohammad Iqbal Naima (based in Dubai), Shamima Shawl (London), and Mukhtar Ahmad Baba (Pakistan) — who are absconding, were charged under BNS Sections 61(2), and 152, alongside Sections 13, 38, 39 and 40 of the UAPA.

articles.title: J&K Finance Assistants exam: 14 held as cheating module busted in Jammu; mobiles, wireless sets seized, say police
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Electronic devices, including wireless radio sets allegedly intended to facilitate the transmission of answers to candidates inside the examination halls, were found and seized by police

A cheating module, planning to employ unfair means by using mobile and wireless devices during the J&K Service Selection Board examination for the posts of Finance Assistants, was busted in Jammu, the J&K Police said on Monday (November 16, 2026).

“The police received information through live sources about people intending to indulge in unfair activity. Different teams were formed and the suspects were followed. articles.title: Trump says ‘would not mind’ Huang being reinstated at Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Trump said Jensen Huang ‘learned a big lesson’ and he ‘would certainly not mind’ if he was reinstated, while adding that there’s a ‘big group of people that would like him to return’

Jensen Huang is reportedly trying to make a comeback as CEO of Nvidia as a campaign to reinstate him picked up steam Monday, with support from tech industry leaders as well as many of the chipmaker's employees.

U.S. President Donald Trump, who has been close with Mr. Huang, also suggested he could return to Nvidia. Mr. Trump said Mr. Huang “learned a big lesson” and he “would certainly not mind” if he was reinstated.
There’s a “big group of people that would like him to return,” Mr. Trump added.
SpaceX and Tesla boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, CEO of video game maker Epic Games, were among thousands of people who signed an online petition calling for Huang to return to the company.

Mr. Huang resigned last week from Nvidia, apparently ousted by the board after revelations that he had extramarital affairs, both with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of being an intelligence asset for Beijing and with a senior executive who reported to him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has stepped in as interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.

Mr. Huang is plotting a comeback, the Financial Times reported over the weekend, citing multiple anonymous sources. The newspaper said he has been discussing the possibility with confidants, as his allies assembled a “war room” of Silicon Valley allies to lobby for his return.

The “Stand with Jensen” petition was set up Friday (November 13) and soon gathered momentum, gaining signatures from current and former Nvidia staff, investors and other supporters. It calls on the board to bring back Mr. Huang while an independent investigation proceeds or there's “compelling evidence” that his departure is in the company's best interests.

“We are concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process,” the petition's organizers said in an open letter. “We do not have access to the Board's private deliberations. We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy.”
The identities of the signatories could not be independently verified, and the website said that their “affiliations are self-reported and not verified.”
Some people posted on their personal accounts that they supported the effort.
“A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too,” Mr. Musk posted on X, while Mr. Sweeney wrote, “Save Jensen!”
Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the petition.

articles.title: India and Egypt form working group to explore trade deal contours
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: India and Egypt have agreed to establish a joint working group to explore the Terms of Reference (ToR) for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement between the two countries, the government announced on Monday (November 16, 2026).

During his ongoing visit to Egypt, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal co-chaired, along with Egypt’s Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade Mohamed Farid Saleh, the 7th session of the India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.
This was the first time this JTC has been convened at the ministerial level.

“As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote investment linkages between the two countries,” the government said in a release.
The release also said that both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of $12 billion.

“Egypt’s proximity to the Suez Canal and its connectivity with African, Arab and European markets make it a valuable partner for export-oriented manufacturing and regional supply chains,” the release said.
“India, in turn, offers Egyptian investors and exporters a large and dynamic market, increasingly competitive infrastructure and opportunities for technology and production partnerships,” it added.

The committee also reviewed the growth in India-Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to $6.5 billion in 2025-26. Trade during the first half of the current financial year (April-September 2026) also stood at a little more than $5 billion, up 65% over its level in the same period of 2025.

articles.title: Divergent positions mark draft text of COP31 under way in Turkiye
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Developing countries call for developed nations to lead emissions cuts and climate finance efforts

Developing countries have called on developed nations to take the lead in achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 and net-negative emissions by 2045, as divergent positions emerged in the draft cover text at the ongoing COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkiye.

Net zero refers to balancing the amount of carbon dioxide emitted with the amount removed from the atmosphere. Several developed countries have set 2050 targets for achieving net-zero emissions, while major developing economies such as India and China have committed to targets of 2070 and 2060, respectively.

The positions of developing countries are largely represented by coalitions such as the Like-Minded Developing Countries (LMDC), which includes India, the Arab Group, the African Group and the Least Developed Countries (LDCs).
Developed-country positions are primarily represented by the European Union, the United Kingdom and Japan. The United States has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement.

The draft cover text also includes a proposal asking developing countries to contribute voluntarily towards climate finance. This funding is intended to help countries adapt to a fossil-fuel-free economy and address losses and damage caused by climate change.

Under the UN climate framework, developed countries, which bear greater historical responsibility for accumulated carbon emissions, are expected to support developing countries through finance and technology as they pursue lower-emission development pathways.

Developing countries have also called for the elimination of measures such as the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) by the end of 2027. The mechanism imposes a tariff on certain imports, including steel, based on the carbon emissions generated during production. Developing countries argue that such measures disadvantage their industries, which often have lower production costs but higher emissions.

Another proposal in the draft concerns a target to source 35% of energy use from electricity by 2035. Some countries have called for there to be no obligation to meet this goal, which was proposed by the COP31 presidency.

COP31 president of negotiations Chris Bowens said the first draft was intended to incorporate proposals from all parties, acknowledging that countries would disagree on certain elements. He said the draft had been released early to ensure transparency and reflect the range of positions.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at activist group 350.org, called for a transition towards renewable energy and electrification, supported by adequate funding. He said the credibility of the climate negotiations depended on leadership in moving away from fossil fuels.

In his first statement at the conference, Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said the global just transition agenda — which involves moving workers from fossil-fuel-based industries towards renewable energy sectors — needed to move beyond dialogue and exchanges of experience towards practical, country-driven implementation. He reiterated India’s commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind.

articles.title: Third American aircraft carrier arrives in West Asia as Trump keeps options open in Iran war
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the Middle East, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three, an unusually high number
The U SS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the West Asia, once again bringing the total number of U.S. aircraft carriers in the West Asia to three — an unusually high number.
A U.S. official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military operations, on Monday (November 16, 2026) confirmed the carrier’s arrival in the region.
It brings thousands of additional troops to the Middle East as President Donald Trump has kept his options open during the more than 8-month-old Iran war.
The Roosevelt, along with its accompanying strike force, left San Diego in September.

The Theodore Roosevelt joins the USS George H.W. Bush and the USS George Washington aircraft carriers, as well as scores of smaller navy ships, that are in the region maintaining a blockade of Iranian shipping. The H.W. Bush arrived in the region in April while the George Washington arrived in August.
According to the Navy, the flotilla in the Arabian Sea now includes three aircraft carriers as well as 13 destroyers, two cruisers and a littoral combat ship.

articles.title: After Yemen setback, Saudi Arabia replaces military commander
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group

Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen’s Iran-allied Houthis ‌on Monday (November 16, 2026) after Riyadh’s Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in ​a major setback for their campaign against the group.

The Houthis have made rapid gains ⁠against the Saudi-backed Yemeni government since the U.S.-Iran conflict reignited Yemen’s frozen civil war this summer, drawing Riyadh back into confrontation with the group.

After gaining ground in a counter-attack in October, the Yemeni government said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) it was withdrawing from ‌areas near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a global shipping artery, to focus on defending its base of operations in Aden, a port city on the southern coast.

People in the Yemeni military ‌said on Monday (November 16, 2026) the Houthis had advanced to the southern coastal area of Khor Omairh, ‌some ⁠100 km (62 miles) west of Aden and were 25 km (16 miles) from government lines at Qawah, ⁠another coastal area.
A royal decree issued by Saudi Arabia’s King Salman spelt out changes to the command of the Saudi-led coalition.

The existing commander, Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad Al-Salman, was appointed as adviser to the defence minister for military affairs, while Chief of ​the General Staff General Fayyad Al-Ruwaili was assigned ‌the additional role of commanding the joint forces, Saudi state media reported.
Two Western diplomats linked the change directly to battlefield developments in Yemen and the Houthi advance.
The Saudi government media office didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports and ‌oil facilities since the Yemen war restarted.
Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on ​Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping have enhanced Iran’s position in the wider Middle East conflict.
Residents of Aden said government security forces had set up more checkpoints and were carrying ⁠out identity checks in the city, the government’s seat of power since the Houthis took Sanaa in 2014.

“Food supplies are available, and so is fuel. However, people are worried about the retreat of government forces and the ‌possibility of fighting drawing closer to Aden,” government employee Amin Mahmoud told Reuters by phone from the city.
