articles.title: Israeli opposition chiefs denounce Netanyahu over ‘attempted coup’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats

Two Israeli opposition leaders denounced Monday (November 16, 2026) an "attempted coup" following press reports that outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office tried to frame members of an Arab-Israeli party ahead of last month's election.

"As more and more details come to light, it becomes clear: This wasn't an attempt to disrupt the elections. It was an attempted coup," wrote Yair Lapid on X, who headed the opposition in the previous legislature and co-chairs the Beyachad list.

Israel's Channel 12 reported Sunday (November 15, 2026) that on the eve of the October 27 election, Mr. Netanyahu's chief of staff Ido Norden had phoned in a complaint to the police about members of the Arab-Israeli Raam party.
Mr. Norden reportedly pointed the police to a purported intelligence source -- a former employee of Mr. Netanyahu's office -- who provided information that led to the arrest of three Raam members.
The three men were later released when the police determined that the information was unfounded.
Mr. Netanyahu subsequently accused Arab parties of electoral fraud after they gained a record number of seats. His Likud party issued a statement denying the latest allegations.

The Israeli newspaper Haaretz also reported that David Zini, head of the Shin Bet domestic security service, sought to wiretap leaders of the other Arab slate, the Joint List, but the attorney general turned down his request due to lack of evidence.
Following the report, Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen also denounced an "attempted coup by Netanyahu".

"If the findings are confirmed, this is a criminal mechanism that operated from the heart of government to rig the election results. Everyone found responsible must be held accountable, including Netanyahu," he wrote on X.
Raam's number two, former police chief Yoav Segalovitz, called for an urgent investigation.
"These suspicions require an immediate, independent and thorough criminal investigation that reaches everyone involved, at every level and in every role," he wrote on X.
"Netanyahu cried out that his election was being stolen, while he himself tried to steal the country and is still trying to do so now," he added.

articles.title: AIIMS Delhi performs a life-changing spinal repair in utero, before the patient’s first breath
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: This is India’s first open foetal repair for myelomeningocele, a defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine; over 30 clinicians and nurses involved in multidisciplinary procedure

The All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi has performed India’s first open foetal repair of a lumbosacral myelomeningocele — the most severe form of spina bifida — at 25 weeks’ gestation.

“The six-hour operation repaired the cerebrospinal-fluid-leaking lumbosacral defect in utero. It followed more than five weeks of multidisciplinary planning, detailed foetal imaging, non-directive counselling, anaesthetic preparation, and operative simulation,’’ AIIMS said in a statement.
A myelomeningocele is an open neural tube defect in which the spinal cord and its coverings protrude through an opening in the spine.

The patient was first screened and counselled by K. Aparna Sharma from the Maternal–Fetal Medicine team. The multidisciplinary procedure was performed using high-end microscopy and continuous high-end ultrasonography assistance at the Neurosciences Centre. The procedure was provided free of cost to the family under the Union government’s Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK).

Deepak Gupta, who led the neurosurgical component, said that the intervention was done after rigorous selection. “Prenatal repair seeks to limit ongoing injury to exposed neural tissue, reduce the subsequent need for cerebrospinal-fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, and improve selected neurological outcomes. It is not a cure, and long-term multidisciplinary care remains essential,” he said.

More than 30 clinicians and nurses from the Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Maternal–Fetal Medicine, Neurosurgery, Obstetrics and Neuroanaesthesia, Plastic Surgery, Radiodiagnosis, Neonatology, and Nursing teams of the Neurosciences Centre and Obstetrics–Gynaecology services participated in the procedure.

Professor Aparna Sharma added that this foetal intervention was well-reasoned and a planned decision aimed to optimise the outcomes of both the baby and the mother. The safety of both mother and foetus was ensured through detailed counselling, high-quality anaesthesia, and coordinated surveillance before and after surgery.

“International trial evidence supports prenatal repair in carefully selected foetuses with open myelomeningocele. The procedure nevertheless carries important maternal and foetal risks, including prematurity and uterine-scar complications, and must be performed only in specialised centres,’’ she said.

The team emphasised that foetal surgery is a treatment for selected pregnancies, not a substitute for prevention. Neural-tube closure occurs by approximately 28 days after conception, often before pregnancy is recognised. Pre-conception folic-acid counselling, evidence-based food fortification with folates, and robust national surveillance remain essential to reducing India’s burden of neural tube defects.

“The mother and foetus will continue to receive close multidisciplinary surveillance through pregnancy, delivery, and the newborn period,’’ the AIIMS statement said, adding that a child with spina bifida may begin life with paralysis, hydrocephalus, and lifelong challenges.

Traditionally, neurosurgeons have done this operation after the child is born. But by then, some of the neurological damage may already have occurred. For some children with spina bifida, the opportunity to protect the spinal cord now begins before birth.

articles.title: Matrescence: when motherhood needs mental health support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: At least one in five women will experience mental health problems during pregnancy until till the first year after childbirth. This cannot be ignored any longer: we need better, more comprehensive policies and programmes to support mothers during this vulnerable period

Monica was not prepared for a caesarean section. She had done everything right and had been assured of a vaginal delivery. Then two weeks before the expected date of delivery, she had to be rushed to the emergency for a caesarean. Monica felt that she had completely lost control of the situation. She found herself alone in an intensive care ward away from her baby, who was in the neonatal ICU and described her birth experience as being extremely traumatic. She is now unable to bond with her baby and keeps questioning herself. Am I such a terrible mother? Will I be like this lifelong?

Priya became pregnant after multiple IVF procedures but did not disclose the pregnancy to anyone till the third trimester, as she didn’t want to jinx it. After a healthy baby girl was born, Priya continued to be anxious and could not trust anyone else to take care of the baby. She would be hypervigilant, and even the smallest change in the infant’s spit-up or breathing would make her panic.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Matrescence: when motherhood needs mental health support. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

Scientific & Technical Core: Innovations led by ISRO, DRDO, CSIR, and national research institutes are advancing India's capabilities in space exploration, quantum computing, biotechnology, and clean energy.

fullParagraphs: A 29-year-old woman from Manuguru, who was rushed to hospital after suddenly losing movement in her right arm and leg, regained significant mobility within hours after doctors at two government hospitals coordinated to administer emergency stroke treatment within the critical window.

Rajani’s ordeal began on an ordinary morning when she suddenly developed slurred speech and complete weakness on her right side. Recognising the signs of an acute stroke, doctors acted swiftly to prevent permanent brain damage.

She was first taken to Area Hospital, Manuguru, where Sai Kumar, a General Medicine specialist, identified the symptoms and arranged an urgent referral to Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, nearly 60 km away, for emergency treatment.

Recognising the narrow window for intervention, M. Ramakrishna, medical superintendent of Area Hospital, Manuguru, coordinated directly with Tejaswi Gadde, physician at Area Hospital, Bhadrachalam, to facilitate her transfer.

At Bhadrachalam, doctors immediately conducted a CT scan to rule out bleeding in the brain before administering clot-dissolving medication. With Rajani still within the recommended 4.5-hour treatment window, doctors administered intravenous Tenecteplase at 2 p.m., around 3.5 hours after the symptoms began, said G. Ravi Babu, District Coordinator of Hospital Services (DCHS), Bhadradri Kothagudem.

The response to treatment was encouraging. Before the intervention, Rajani had no detectable movement in her right arm or leg, with her muscle power recorded at 0/5. Following thrombolysis, her muscle strength improved, and she regained the ability to move the affected limbs against resistance, though full strength is yet to return.

She remains under close neurological observation. The case also highlights the availability of advanced emergency treatment in government hospitals serving remote and tribal areas. The thrombolytic medication, which costs around ₹45,000 in the market, was administered to Rajani free of cost.

Dr. Ravi Babu appreciated the doctors, nurses and supporting staff at both hospitals for their prompt decisions and coordination. “Such interventions demonstrate how teamwork between government healthcare institutions can help deliver advanced, life-saving treatment even in geographically remote areas,” he said.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: This year’s Booker Prize betrays an anxiety about AI’s place in society

A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The overturning of the mandate in the Gokul Dairy cooperative is disturbing

Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

✍️ Editorial & Opinion 📅 15 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Caste and class: On OBC reservation

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary

Exclusion of creamy layer is essential, but must be done consistently

If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: CM promises govt. support to India’s newest public health university coming up in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy assured the Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI) of the State government’s full support for establishing its Institute of Public Health Sciences (IPHS) Deemed-to-be University in Hyderabad, setting June 2, 2028, as the deadline for completing the proposed campus and promising assistance with land, funds, permissions and other requirements.

Speaking at the foundation-laying ceremony and unveiling of the campus master plan on Saturday, Mr. Reddy said the government was committed to developing the institution into a world-class university that would contribute to public health education, research and healthcare in India and internationally.

He further added that the proposed university was not merely another educational institution but a project of global significance. Expressing confidence in its potential, he said he hoped that in the coming years, people would discuss the PHFI university alongside established institutions such as Harvard and Oxford.

The Chief Minister recalled how institutions such as the Indian School of Business (ISB) had contributed to Hyderabad’s emergence as an educational and knowledge hub. He said individuals who had established successful institutions had helped create a distinct identity for the city and that the PHFI university would add to this legacy.
PHFI Chairman Rajat Gupta said the university aspired to achieve excellence through world-class faculty, students, international collaborations and infrastructure.

PHFI IPHS Chancellor Dr. K. Srinath Reddy said PHFI aspired to become the world’s leading public health institution with the establishment of the university in Hyderabad. Dr. Reddy said the foundation’s work involved advancing multidisciplinary education and research through multi-sectoral implementation and multi-stakeholder engagement. The objective was to improve life expectancy, strengthen health systems, align policies across sectors with population health goals and encourage active community engagement.

Pro-Chancellor Sanjay Zodpey said the university was being conceived as a long-term institution that would serve generations of students, researchers, public health professionals and communities. He said the public health challenges of the 21st century required professionals with interdisciplinary perspectives, evidence-based knowledge and a commitment to equity and social impact.

Vice-Chancellor M. Vishnu Vardhana Rao outlined the university’s academic journey and expansion plans. The Indian Institute of Public Health Hyderabad was established in 2008 under the aegis of PHFI, with the objective of advancing public health through education, research and community engagement. The institution received recognition as a deemed-to-be university from the University Grants Commission in 2025, with Hyderabad as its main campus and Bengaluru as another campus, he said.

With the proposed campus and modern infrastructure, the institution plans to expand its academic offerings to at least six postgraduate programmes, two undergraduate programmes, PhD programmes and institute-level Master of Public Health programmes. It aims to build an academic community of approximately 2,500 students and research scholars over the next five years.

Dr. Rao said the university’s research priorities would include infectious diseases and pandemic preparedness, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, One Health, mental health and disability. Digital health, artificial intelligence and data science would serve as cross-cutting areas across its research activities, he added.

articles.title: Synod of Jacobite Church approves steps to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Episcopal Synod of the Jacobite Syrian Church on Saturday (November 14) decided to complete the procedures to canonise Patriarch Ignatius Peter III, who convened the historic Mulanthuruthy Synod in 1876. The decision was taken as Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, the supreme head of the Universal Syrian Orthodox Church, accepted the Jacobite Church’s request to declare Ignatius Peter III a saint.

A statement by the Jacobite Syrian Church said the decision was taken at a meeting of the Episcopal Synod, chaired by Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II, at the Marthoman Cathedral in Mulanthuruthy during the 150th anniversary celebrations of the Mulanthuruthy Synod.
Addressing the synod, the Patriarch called for collective efforts to establish lasting peace in the Malankara Church.
Hailing from Mosul, Ignatius Peter III was the Patriarch of Antioch and head of the Syriac Orthodox Church from 1872 until he died in 1894.

articles.title: Police intensify investigation in sexual harassment case against TVK functionary
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: TVK’s Karamadai union secretary Karupusamy, party worker Sabitha, and her husband Pandi are the accused in the case

The Coimbatore District Police have intensified investigation into the allegations by a woman functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) that Karamadai union secretary of the party sexually harassed her in May this year.

Coimbatore District Superintendent of Police A. Pavan Kumar Reddy said the investigating officer would also verify some of the audio tapes and videos, which the complainant had claimed as evidence to back her allegations. TVK’s Karamadai union secretary Karupusamy, party worker Sabitha, and her husband Pandi are the three accused in the case.

The complainant, aged 29, who formerly held the post of the party’s secretary at a panchayat in Karamadai union, has alleged that she was removed from her post after she questioned Karupusamy over the alleged sexual harassment. The two others, she has alleged, harassed her on caste grounds.

Lawyer N. Panneerselvam of Samooga Neethi Katchi, who has been offering legal assistance to the complainant, alleged that the police were not keen on arresting the accused despite having registered a case against them for serious offences. “We were told the accused are at large. It is the duty of the police to trace them. Legal support will be offered to the complainant if they [accused] move for anticipatory bail,” he said.
The police, however, refused to state whether the trio was on the run.

Meanwhile, a video of the woman complaining about the harassment to MLA N. Sunil Anand before the case was registered has surfaced. As the woman was talking to him, the MLA is seen in the video telling others that “it was not an important thing”. The woman had claimed in her complaint to the police that she had reported the incident to the MLA thrice.

articles.title: BJP to stage protest against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA on Nov. 18
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: State govt. failed to act on complaints against MLA who allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the Collector, says BJP
The BJP will hold a demonstration in Kallakurichi on November 18 against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh, who had allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the district Collector.
State BJP president Nainar Nagenthran told journalists in Chennai on Saturday that the protest will be led by former Telangana Governor Tamilisai Soundararajan.

Addressing reporters at Kamalalayam, the party headquarters, Mr. Nagenthran alleged the State government had failed to act on complaints relating to the case and demanded accountability from the ruling government.

He said the BJP wanted a special court to ensure an effective investigation into the allegations. He also urged the Madras High Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter, alleging that complaints had not been acted upon despite being brought to the attention of the authorities.

Questioning Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s response to the allegations, Mr. Nagenthran said the Chief Minister had the responsibility to act both as the head of the government and as the leader of the ruling party. He also criticised the responses of Ministers and leaders of the Congress party to the issue.

Mr. Nagenthran accused the State government of failing to maintain law and order and alleged that incidents involving crimes against women and children had increased in the past six months. Referring to reports of missing children, including seven girls among 12 persons reported missing in Cuddalore district, he questioned the government’s response to concerns over women’s safety.

On the State’s industrial performance, he alleged Tamil Nadu was losing investments to neighbouring States because of a deterioration in law and order and a lack of investor confidence. Citing a proposed investment of ₹15,000 crore by a Hyundai group company in Andhra Pradesh, he said the government should address the concerns of industries.

He also claimed the State’s GST revenue growth had declined from 5% to minus 5% and attributed this to manufacturing units moving to neighbouring States. He urged the Chief Minister to take immediate steps to address the situation.
Earlier on Saturday, over 100 persons, including members of the Congress and other political parties, joined the BJP at the party headquarters in the presence of senior functionaries.

State govt. failed to act on complaints against MLA who allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the Collector, says BJP

The BJP will hold a demonstration in Kallakurichi on November 18 against TVK’s Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh, who had allegedly sent inappropriate messages to the district Collector.

State BJP president Nainar Nagenthran told journalists in Chennai on Saturday that the protest will be led by former Telangana Governor Tamilisai Soundararajan.

Addressing reporters at Kamalalayam, the party headquarters, Mr. Nagenthran alleged the State government had failed to act on complaints relating to the case and demanded accountability from the ruling government.

He said the BJP wanted a special court to ensure an effective investigation into the allegations. He also urged the Madras High Court to take suo motu cognisance of the matter, alleging that complaints had not been acted upon despite being brought to the attention of the authorities.

Questioning Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s response to the allegations, Mr. Nagenthran said the Chief Minister had the responsibility to act both as the head of the government and as the leader of the ruling party. He also criticised the responses of Ministers and leaders of the Congress party to the issue.

Mr. Nagenthran accused the State government of failing to maintain law and order and alleged that incidents involving crimes against women and children had increased in the past six months. Referring to reports of missing children, including seven girls among 12 persons reported missing in Cuddalore district, he questioned the government’s response to concerns over women’s safety.

On the State’s industrial performance, he alleged Tamil Nadu was losing investments to neighbouring States because of a deterioration in law and order and a lack of investor confidence. Citing a proposed investment of ₹15,000 crore by a Hyundai group company in Andhra Pradesh, he said the government should address the concerns of industries.

He also claimed the State’s GST revenue growth had declined from 5% to minus 5% and attributed this to manufacturing units moving to neighbouring States. He urged the Chief Minister to take immediate steps to address the situation.

Earlier on Saturday, over 100 persons, including members of the Congress and other political parties, joined the BJP at the party headquarters in the presence of senior functionaries.

articles.title: Driver from Theni found dead while in custody at Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Amid outrage over the custodial death, an Inspector of the Chekkanoorani police station and two police constables have been placed under suspension

A truck driver from Theni district, R. Balakrishnan, who was being questioned at the Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai in connection with a container truck fire, died in custody on Saturday morning. The police claimed he was found dead in the restroom on the station premises.

Amid outrage over the custodial death, Muthu, Inspector of the Chekkanoorani police station, and two police constables were placed under suspension. The case was transferred to the Crime Branch-CID for further investigation and Balakrishnan’s body was taken to the Government Rajaji Hospital.

A statement from the Madurai District Police said Balakrishnan had submitted a complaint that his truck had caught fire near Valandur on November 3, destroying the cardamom bags stored in its container. Based on the complaint, the Valandur police registered a case of accidental fire on Friday evening. Balakrishnan was then detained at the Chekkanoorani police station for inquiry.
The statement claimed that he was detained at the station to assist the Investigating Officer in verifying CCTV camera footage related to the case.
The police claimed that Balakrishnan had gone to the restroom at 6 a.m. on Saturday and attempted to end his life.
The police found him unconscious in the restroom and rushed him to a hospital in Madurai, where the doctor declared him brought dead.
However, his wife Sudha claimed that Balakrishnan had been questioned by the police on Thursday too, and the inquiry had resumed for the second day on Friday.

“I had accompanied him to the police station on the previous day (Thursday). He was questioned there from 6 p.m. till 11.30 p.m. He was asked to come again the next day,” she said, crying inconsolably. She regretted not having accompanied her husband to the police station on Friday.
Ms. Sudha charged that her husband was “fixed” in the case in which he himself was the complainant, as the value of the cardamom destroyed in the fire was high.

Stating that Balakrishnan had recorded a video of the truck fire on his mobile phone and even the owner of the vehicle had rushed to the spot of the accident, she complained that police personnel had detained only Balakrishnan at the station on Friday.

Balakrishnan’s family members alleged that his prolonged detention and overnight questioning by the police over an accidental fire that was reported nearly 10 days ago was baffling. They also asserted that Balakrishnan was a bold person and refused to accept the police’s version that the driver had taken his own life.

“How can a man who is over five-and-a-half-foot tall end his life inside a bathroom that is only six-foot high?” an advocate asked. He also sought the CCTV camera footage of the police station from the day Balakrishnan’s questioning started to the time of his death.

articles.title: Investment promotion panel holds first meeting, targets $72 billion in exports
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Discussions also focused on the proposed new industrial policy, single-window clearances, and MoUs inked since the TVK-led government came to power

The first meeting of the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion Commission (TNIPC) was held under the chairmanship of Chief Secretary Sai Kumar, with discussions focusing on the proposed new industrial policy, single-window clearances, progress of investment MoUs, and measures to boost the State’s exports.

During the meeting, the preparatory work for the New Industrial Policy 2027 was reviewed. “Consultations with various stakeholders have been undertaken since July 2026. The existing industrial policies are also being evaluated to identify areas requiring revision and improvement. Directions have been issued to expedite the preparation of the new policy,” a statement issued by the Industries Department said.

There were discussions around the Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) inked ever since the TVK government came to power. Since May 2026, the government has signed 112 MoUs, representing proposed investments exceeding ₹1.14 lakh crore and the potential to generate employment for 1,32,771 persons. Of these, 83 MoUs have progressed to land allotment and beyond. The overall implementation progress currently stands at 74.11%.

An official release said the commission discussed measures to help Tamil Nadu’s industries leverage the opportunities emerging from India’s Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), expand their international market presence, and increase exports.

The State aims to increase its exports from the present $59 billion to $72 billion. The Commission also issued directions to all departments. It said that all departments must ensure that applications covered under the amended Business Facilitation Act are processed within the mandatory 21-day timeline.

It has said the Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) should establish a mechanism to expedite the processing of applications for High Tension (HT) and Extra High Tension (EHT) connections for industrial units. The Commission emphasised the need to conduct export promotion and facilitation meetings at the district level, in addition to State-level meetings. With all these initiatives, Tamil Nadu intends to become a $1.5 trillion economy by 2036.

The Commission was constituted on November 3, 2026, under Section 16 A of the Tamil Nadu Business Facilitation Act, 2018, as amended through the Tamil Nadu Investment Promotion and Facilitation Legislation, 2026. The Commission is chaired by the Chief Secretary, with the Additional Chief Secretary, Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce Department, serving as its Member Secretary and Convener. It comprises 20 members representing various key government departments, including Finance, Energy, Information Technology, Housing and Urban Development, Transport, Environment, Labour Welfare and Commercial Taxes, among others.

The Commission will provide focused attention to major investment proposals involving investments of ₹200 crore and above, projects generating 5,000 or more employment opportunities, and projects requiring inter departmental coordination for expeditious implementation. It will also facilitate the opportunities arising from India’s Free Trade Agreements (FTAs).

articles.title: Three arrested in Bhopal for duping Delhi woman of ₹71 lakh in ‘digital arrest’ scam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The accused impersonated an IPS officer and threatened the victim with arrest in a fake ₹6.5-crore money laundering case; IFSO uncovers a network of mule bank accounts used to route the cheated money

Three persons from Madhya Pradesh’s Bhopal have been arrested for duping a woman of ₹71 lakh by impersonating an IPS officer and threatening her with arrest in a digital arrest scam, officials from Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit of the Delhi Police said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

The accused, identified as Priyanka Prajapati (31), Aman Soni (28) and Pinky Soni (30), were arrested from Bhopal in Madhya Pradesh by the IFSO officials. The investigation also unearthed a network of mule bank accounts used to receive and divert money obtained through cyber fraud.

According to the police, the victim received a WhatsApp video call from a person posing as an IPS officer posted in Mumbai. The caller told her that a credit card had been issued in her name and was being used for money laundering involving transactions worth approximately ₹6.5 crore.

The fraudster threatened to arrest her and send her to judicial custody, and coerced her into transferring money under the pretext of verification to avoid legal action. Under fear and intimidation, the woman transferred ₹71 lakh in two transactions, the police said.
An e-FIR was registered at the Special Cell police station on October 8, following which the IFSO unit took up the investigation.

During the probe, the police traced the financial trail and identified multiple bank accounts allegedly used to receive and divert the cheated money. The three accused were part of this network and facilitated the movement and withdrawal of the funds in coordination with other handlers.

The police said approximately ₹15 lakh was withdrawn and distributed among the accused and their associates. A portion of the cheated money was also allegedly used to purchase expensive mobile phones.
Three newly purchased mobile phones, suspected to have been bought using the defrauded money, have been recovered from the accused.
Further investigation is underway to identify the larger network involved in the fraud and tracing the proceeds of the crime.

articles.title: Flight services on Imphal-Silchar route scheduled to commence on November 24
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The services will be operated by Alliance Air under the Viability Gap Funding facility and flight frequency would be two days a week, every Tuesday and Thursday, an airport official said
Flight services on the Imphal-Silchar route are scheduled to commence on November 24, an airport official said in Imphal on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The services will be operated by Alliance Air under the Viability Gap Funding facility, he said, adding that flight frequency would be two days a week, every Tuesday and Thursday.
"This is a positive step towards strengthening regional air connectivity and facilitating passenger movement between Imphal and Silchar," the official said.

The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) Scheme was launched in October 2016 with the objective of making air travel affordable and enhancing regional air connectivity, particularly to tier-II and tier-III cities.
To support airline operators and encourage sustained route development, the scheme continues the provision of Viability Gap Funding.

articles.title: Maharashtra government urges drought-hit farmers to complete e-KYC, obtain Farmer IDs to access benefits
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the department, completing the necessary registration and verification procedures is essential for eligible beneficiaries to receive funds directly in their bank accounts

The Maharashtra government’s Relief and Rehabilitation Department on Saturday (November 14) urged drought-affected farmers across the State to complete their e-KYC verification and obtain Farmer IDs at the earliest to ensure they can access financial assistance and benefits under various Central and State government schemes.

The appeal comes in the wake of the State government’s decision to provide advance financial assistance to drought-affected farmers before Diwali. According to the department, completing the necessary registration and verification procedures is essential for eligible beneficiaries to receive funds directly in their bank accounts.

In a statement, the department said farmers must ensure that their information is updated on the AgriStack platform, which maintains updated farmer information and facilitates the delivery of benefits under agricultural and other government welfare schemes.

The department said the government has provided financial assistance to farmers during various crises in the past and continues to extend support through subsidies and other schemes. It added that completing e-KYC verification and obtaining a Farmer ID would help minimise difficulties in accessing assistance and facilitate the timely transfer of benefits to eligible farmers.

The State government also assured farmers that necessary assistance would be provided to resolve technical or other difficulties encountered during registration and verification. Farmers facing such issues have been advised to contact the relevant authorities rather than leave their applications incomplete.
To obtain a Farmer ID, farmers have been asked to visit their nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) with their Aadhaar card and Aadhaar-linked mobile number to complete the registration process.

The department reiterated that updating farmer records and completing verification procedures were important to ensure the timely and transparent distribution of government benefits. It urged farmers across Maharashtra, particularly those affected by drought, to prioritise the process and complete the required formalities without delay.

articles.title: In major breakthrough, U.S. assures India of comparative tariff advantage over its competitors
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: So far, Indian government officials have been maintaining that India would move ahead with a trade deal with the U.S. only if such a comparative advantage is assured

In a significant breakthrough towards the conclusion of the India-U.S. interim deal on trade, the U.S. has assured India of a comparative advantage over its competitors once it finalises its tariff structure, a senior official in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry said, adding that both sides are working to complete the deal by the end of the current financial year.
U.S. must respect India’s right to defend itself, maintain zero tolerance towards terrorism: Blinken

Indian officials have repeatedly been saying that India would move ahead with a deal only if the U.S. assured it of a comparative advantage, as was agreed to in the February 2026 joint statement between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and U.S. President Donald Trump.

Separately, Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal confirmed that a two-man team from the U.S. visited India earlier this month during which substantial progress was made towards finalising the text of the deal.

“Talks between India and the U.S. are ongoing and the U.S. has assured us of a comparative advantage over our competitor countries,” the senior official said on the condition of anonymity as the details of the bilateral discussions have not yet been made public.

This is a significant development because Indian officials, including Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, have repeatedly said that India would move ahead with a deal with the U.S. only if it is assured of a comparative advantage over its competitors.
The February joint statement stated that the U.S. and India “commit to provide each other preferential market access in sectors of respective interest on a sustained basis”.

However, since then, the U.S. has imposed additional 10% ‘forced labour’ tariffs on India, the same as on some of its competitors such as Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Further, the U.S. is currently conducting another investigation into India and several other countries related to excess capacity, which could see additional tariffs being levied.
The official, however, said that the U.S. assurance of comparative advantage for India takes into account this future tariff.

“The attempt by both sides is to complete the deal by the end of this financial year,” the official added. “We have also agreed to a clause that says that if either country changes its tariffs on the other country, then the second country can also modify its commitments under the deal. This was also a part of the February joint statement.”
The official said that such a clause is “not usual” in trade deals that India enters into, but that it had specifically been included in the deal with the U.S.
Separately, Mr. Agrawal said that the talks between the two sides were “on the right track” and that the teams are engaged both in-person and virtually.

articles.title: PNB fund misappropriation case: Bank says genuine claims to be honoured, FIR registered in Gr Noida
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The bank said it was extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and taking necessary steps to address the concerns of affected customers

Punjab National Bank (PNB) on Thursday (October 29, 2026) assured customers that all genuine claims would be honoured and said it had settled three claims amounting to ₹43 lakh in connection with alleged financial irregularities involving savings accounts and fixed deposits at its Greater Noida branch.
The bank said it was examining the complaints on priority and verifying the facts to assess the extent of the reported discrepancies.
“Three claims amounting to ₹43 lakh had been settled as of yesterday. The Bank assures its customers that all genuine claims will be honoured,” PNB said in a statement.
The bank said it was extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and taking necessary steps to address the concerns of affected customers.

It reiterated its zero-tolerance policy towards fraud, financial irregularities and misconduct, adding that strict action would be taken against those found responsible in accordance with applicable rules and procedures. The bank also said it was strengthening internal controls and monitoring mechanisms to prevent a recurrence of such incidents.

The development comes after nearly two dozen account holders alleged misappropriation of funds totalling more than ₹11.24 crore from their savings accounts and fixed deposits at the branch. An FIR has been registered against unidentified bank employees under Section 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with criminal breach of trust, following a complaint by customer Shrichand and other account holders.
According to the complaint, the alleged losses listed for 21 individuals exceed ₹11.24 crore, with two account holders claiming losses of more than ₹1 crore each.
Separately, local account holders have estimated the total alleged fraud at around ₹35 crore, claiming that savings accounts, fixed deposits and mutual fund investments were affected.
Shrichand, a resident of Surajpur in Greater Noida, alleged that bank employees misappropriated ₹1.16 crore from his fixed deposit.

Other account holders named in the complaint include Kartari, Amichand, Vijay Pal, Santosh, Saroj, Bijendra Singh, Ranpal, Dharm Singh, Haneep Khan, Sonu, Jagdish, Sunita, Akash Bhati, Atender, Chatar Singh, Vinit Bhati, Sanjay, Basanti, and Gajendra.

Bijendra Singh, another account holder, told reporters that his savings account, which had held Rs 87-88 lakh, now showed a balance of only ₹1 lakh. A farmer, he said the money included compensation received from an authority.

Haneep Khan alleged that nearly ₹39 lakh had disappeared from his account without authorisation, while another account holder, Zakir, claimed that ₹9.5 lakh was missing and that he had received no text message alerting him to any transaction.

It reiterated its zero-tolerance policy towards fraud, financial irregularities and misconduct, adding that strict action would be taken against those found responsible in accordance with applicable rules and procedures. The bank also said it was strengthening internal controls and monitoring mechanisms to prevent a recurrence of such incidents.

The development comes after nearly two dozen account holders alleged misappropriation of funds totalling more than ₹11.24 crore from their savings accounts and fixed deposits at the branch. An FIR has been registered against unidentified bank employees under Section 316(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with criminal breach of trust, following a complaint by customer Shrichand and other account holders.

According to the complaint, the alleged losses listed for 21 individuals exceed ₹11.24 crore, with two account holders claiming losses of more than ₹1 crore each.

Separately, local account holders have estimated the total alleged fraud at around ₹35 crore, claiming that savings accounts, fixed deposits and mutual fund investments were affected.

Shrichand, a resident of Surajpur in Greater Noida, alleged that bank employees misappropriated ₹1.16 crore from his fixed deposit.

Other account holders named in the complaint include Kartari, Amichand, Vijay Pal, Santosh, Saroj, Bijendra Singh, Ranpal, Dharm Singh, Haneep Khan, Sonu, Jagdish, Sunita, Akash Bhati, Atender, Chatar Singh, Vinit Bhati, Sanjay, Basanti, and Gajendra.

Bijendra Singh, another account holder, told reporters that his savings account, which had held Rs 87-88 lakh, now showed a balance of only ₹1 lakh. A farmer, he said the money included compensation received from an authority.

Haneep Khan alleged that nearly ₹39 lakh had disappeared from his account without authorisation, while another account holder, Zakir, claimed that ₹9.5 lakh was missing and that he had received no text message alerting him to any transaction.

articles.title: Indian student jailed for 30 years for online child sex abuse in U.K.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15

A 27-year-old Indian student described by U.K. authorities as a “serial online groomer” was sentenced to 30 years’ imprisonment in north-west England on Friday (November 13, 2026) for “exploiting and coercing” several children online to commit sexual acts.

Bilal Kazi was sentenced at Chester Crown Court after pleading guilty to a series of child sexual abuse offences committed online. The court heard that Kazi pretended to be a teenage boy on social media and gaming platforms to build trust with girls aged between 10 and 15.

“Bilal Kazi acted with absolute ruthlessness in grooming, manipulating and exploiting a large number of young vulnerable girls," said Martin McRobb, Specialist Prosecutor at the U.K.’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

“He befriended them online and forced them to take photos and videos of them carrying out sexual acts. He then blackmailed those who refused to comply with his further demands, threatening to post the explicit imagery to others.

“He posed as a teenage boy in order to attract and gain the trust of his victims and caused many to think that they were in a genuine relationship with him. When the victims realised they had been deceived, they were understandably distressed, and some suffered serious and long-term trauma," he said.
The CPS said its Organised Child Sexual Abuse Unit presented the court with overwhelming evidence gathered by police investigators in Cheshire and the West Midlands.

“The scale of Kazi’s offending meant this was a truly mammoth investigation, requiring significant resources and close collaboration across the force,” said Detective Constable Georgia Hughes, of the Online Child Abuse Investigation Team at Cheshire Constabulary.

“The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable. For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship. Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal.

“His offending has had a profound and lasting impact on the victims. Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years. What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse," he said.

According to the police force, the first victim explained that she began speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age. Their conversations quickly turned explicit in nature, with Kazi asking the victim several inappropriate questions.

“I hope this case demonstrates our commitment to protecting vulnerable people and bringing an end to the sexual exploitation of children. It should also serve as a warning to those who, like Kazi, believe that hiding behind a screen makes them anonymous and untouchable," said Detective Sergeant Ross Peel of the Constabulary.

According to the British authorities, in July 2021, the victim told Kazi that she only wanted to be friends and no longer wished to send him images. In response, Kazi became abusive, calling her names and claiming that she was his property. He then threatened to distribute the photos and videos she had previously shared with him to her friends unless she obeyed his demands. Fearing Kazi’s threats, the victim felt compelled to continue sending him explicit images and videos.

articles.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2

Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday (November 14, 2026) pulled off the first-ever “catch” of a spaceship, a technical feat showing the feasibility of fully reusable rockets that would bring affordable spaceflight one step closer to reality.

The Starship emerged from the clouds after surviving the extreme heat of re-entering Earth’s atmosphere, then descended slowly over SpaceX’s south Texas Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2.

The success marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems -- a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible.
“That was the Holy Grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said.

Crowds outside Starbase broke into ecstatic cheers as the spaceship came into view, with the 1977 soft rock hit “Baby Come Back” serving as the soundtrack of the nerve-wracking final descent on SpaceX’s official livestream.

“I really do believe this is the dawn of the space age,” said Dane Walter, 38, a spectator who came from Corpus Christi, Texas. “And truly, I consider it an equivalent moment to the Wright brothers at Kitty Hawk.”

It was the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. Up until now, spaceships have been single-use items, discarded or destroyed after missions, making each launch an expensive resource-intensive venture.
The Starship spacecraft that gives SpaceX’s rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink internet constellation during its 22-hour journey.

SpaceX had previously captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was more complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude compared to boosters.
“I hugged ship 42 upon its return,” Mr. Musk posted on X about the captured vessel, sharing videos taken from various angles and saying it “looks great!”

Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.”
Analyst Kathleen Curlee hailed the achievement but said there was more work to be done.

articles.title: NATO to skip a leaders' summit in Albania next year as high-level meetings are scaled back
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he said

NATO is scaling back its high-level meetings and will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year as previously planned amid tension within the alliance over defence spending, Iran and the war in Ukraine.

Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that “there is not yet a common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027.” He said that “in 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana,” Albania's capital.

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte played down the issue. “We are flexible with NATO summits,” he told The Associated Press in an interview. “We have summits when we need them,” he said, and will hold the next one “when a necessity is there.”
Until about a decade ago, NATO held summits every two years.
It's not just about gatherings between U.S. President Donald Trump and his counterparts.

NATO Defence Ministers usually meet in October, but no talks took place last month, and none are planned for October 2027. Foreign Ministers only have one scheduled meeting next year, instead of two, under what NATO describes as a “reorganization package.”

U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have each skipped a NATO meeting or left before talks ended since they came to office. Mr. Hegseth has used defence ministerial gatherings to berate or cajole European allies and Canada.
The planned summit in Albania highlights the alliance's challenges. Albania was appointed next year's host in 2025, but its name was removed from a July summit declaration.

Some allies believe that Albania is not spending enough on defence and they were reluctant to reward the country with NATO's big event. The government in Tirana is projected to spend 2.15% of its gross domestic product on defense this year.

NATO's target is for the 32 allies to spend 3.5% of GDP on core defense by 2035, and 1.5% on defense-related infrastructure. Albania is not the worst offender among the 32 member countries. Spain, Belgium and Slovenia are faring much worse.
But hosting a summit itself has tremendous financial and political costs. The Netherlands required a year of preparation ahead of the 2025 meeting in The Hague, and a roughly $100 million investment.
Officials said NATO would have needed to decide on Albania by October for it to have enough time to organize a summit next year.

articles.title: Ebola outbreak remains out of control in Congo six months into response
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Ebola outbreak is the deadliest of Congo’s 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016
Six months after an Ebola outbreak was declared in Congo, the disease remains out of control and efforts to contain it are faltering.

More than 11,000 cases have been recorded, and nearly half of those infected have died, according to Government data. It is the deadliest of Congo's 17 outbreaks and is on track to surpass the death toll from the West African outbreak that killed 11,000 people between 2014 and 2016.

Basic containment measures, including contact tracing and isolation, remain inadequate, raising doubts about authorities' ability to halt the outbreak. Experts say there is little chance of bringing it under control within the next year.

By the time the outbreak was announced in mid-May, 43 deaths had already been recorded, suggesting the virus had circulated undetected for an extended period. It has since spread to eight of the country's 26 provinces, moving at a pace aid groups have likened to wildfire.
New hotspots continue to emerge, stretching an already strained health care system.

Community transmission remains high. According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, 80% of new cases are being detected outside health surveillance, meaning most infections have not been tracked by authorities.
Experts warn of wider spread as Ebola outbreak reaches plateau
DR Congo Ebola outbreak exceeds 11,000 cases, causes 5,387 deaths
Congo's Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as disease keeps spreading
One-third of deaths occur at home or elsewhere in the community, where burials and other procedures are often conducted without specialist supervision, increasing the risk of transmission.
Health workers have repeatedly gone on strike over pay that is months overdue, sometimes leaving patients with confirmed infections without treatment.
Aid groups have also questioned how the response is being managed. Last month, the Africa CDC raised concerns about more than $700 million in Ebola aid that remains unaccounted for.

articles.title: U.S. suggested Kyiv cede land to Russia in exchange for joining NATO, says Zelenskyy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign
Mr. Zelenskyy also warned the Kremlin was “betting everything” on this winter’s military campaign.
Moscow has pounded Ukraine in the run-up to the colder months, with Russian President Vladimir Putin showing no sign of backing down.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met both Mr. Putin and Mr. Zelenskyy separately on Thursday after two days of talks with their delegations in Abu Dhabi, which ended with no breakthrough.
“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?’ This was the first time this had been raised,” Mr. Zelenskyy said.
“After providing Ukraine with this kind of defence support, seeing this kind of development of our army and this strength in our defence, they cannot simply let Ukraine go,” he added.
He said the discussion showed that “NATO is back on the agenda” for Ukraine.
Ukraine has long sought to enter the military alliance, which Moscow has considered a red line.
NATO and Washington have not yet commented directly on Mr. Zelenskyy’s account.
Mr. Kushner, U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, later posted on X that media had reported “maximalist propositions proposed by both sides, along with strong political rhetoric”.

“However, we are determined to continue the hard work, maintain the confidentiality necessary for sensitive negotiations, and find a pathway to end this horrible war,” he said, adding “several new ideas emerged from the discussions and are now being explored.”
This week’s meetings have led to agreements that European countries would join future talks on ending the war.
In Dublin on Friday (November 13, 2026), Europe chose five countries — France, Germany, Italy, the U.K. and Poland — to send representatives to the talks.

articles.title: Cape Verde could elect first woman President since gaining independence in 1975
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes
Cape Verde could elect its first woman President on Sunday (November 15, 2026) as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is seeking a second term.
Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes.

Ms. Rosa, backed by the Opposition Movement for Democracy, is the first woman to run for President since independence from Portugal in 1975. Women have held senior cabinet posts, but Cape Verde has never had a female prime minister or president.

In Cape Verde's parliamentary system, the Prime Minister directs government policy and holds most executive authority. The president's role is largely symbolic, although the directly elected head of state can veto legislation.

The Atlantic island nation off West Africa, home to about half a million people, has a record of peaceful transfers of power and competitive elections in a region where that is rare. Nearly 77,000 Cape Verdeans abroad are registered to vote, almost a fifth of the total electorate.

Many voters feel distant from their leaders and want a president who understands their daily difficulties, while limited economic prospects were driving young people to seek opportunities abroad, said Roselma Evora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde.
Mr. Neves, who won in 2021 with about 52% of the vote, has pledged to build cross-party support to improve housing, healthcare and education, create jobs and raise wages.
Incumbency gives Mr. Neves greater visibility, including among overseas voters, Evora said.
Ms. Rosa's candidacy challenges traditional expectations of women's roles in a society that remains “very patriarchal,” Evora said.

Ms. Rosa has centred her campaign on maintaining a balance of power, arguing that the country needs a counterweight to the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde, which backs Neves and controls the government and most municipalities.

Known as PAICV, the party won a parliamentary majority in May, ending a decade of government led by the Movement for Democracy. A Rosa victory would again put the presidency and government in rival political camps.
Rosário Luz, a Cape Verde-based writer, said party loyalties mattered more than Ms. Rosa's gender.

articles.title: What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure .

This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions .
Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness.

As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community.

Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs.

Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household.

Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health.

Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .”

But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.
When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”
Since then, thousands of community organizations like Community Servings and Project Open Hand have provided healthy food to vulnerable community members.

In 2023, the president of the American Heart Association convened an advisory group of researchers and physicians to review current food is medicine research and suggest next steps for work in this area. This advisory has suggested that these programs could help prevent or manage chronic conditions, saving the U.S. healthcare system an estimated US$4.3 trillion annually .

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred
People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found.

Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age.
Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said.

"Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy.

Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes.

"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said.

"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.
